As replacements for the heavily aged Kiha 17 series (including the Kiha 44000 series) and the postal and baggage cars converted from the Kiha 55 series, conversion cars reusing the underframes and running gear of surplus Kiro 28s appeared from fiscal 1977. The all-compartment baggage car was the Kini 28 and the postal-baggage car the Kiyuni 28.

The bodies were newly built, of the same type as the Kiha 40 series built at the same period. As air-conditioning units were not fitted, the 4DQ power equipment and one each of the KE53 air-conditioning-control and KE8 high-voltage power-supply jumper couplers were removed. The conversions were carried out from 1978 at Nagoya, Tadotsu, Hata, Koriyama and Takasago Works, with Koriyama and Takasago handling the Kiyuni 28 only.

The Kini 28 had a baggage room of 12 t load behind the cab, with baggage shelves and a valuables box, and a baggage conductor's room, toilet and washroom at the rear car end.

The Kiyuni 28 had a 6 t postal room on the front side and a 6 t baggage room on the rear side, with toilet and washroom on the rear side face and the rear end face.

The livery of the first-delivered Kiyuni 28 1–6 was the general color of cream No. 4 and vermilion No. 4, but the other six cars were changed to the Tokyo metropolitan-area color of vermilion No. 5 following the October 1978 revision of the "Vehicle Livery and Marking Standards".

They were allocated throughout Japan except Hokkaido, but as railway postal and baggage transport was abolished at the November 1986 (Showa 61) timetable revision, less than ten years after conversion, all cars were scrapped by the following year, and not one car was inherited by the JR Group.

Kiro 28 78, 58, 53, 73, 122 → Kini 28 1–6

Kiro 28 199, 132, 200, 119, 70, 176, 85, 129, 57, 29, 501, 67, 33, 34, 20, 49, 12, 145, 146, 106, 37, 48, 153, 38, 121, 54, 81, 36 → Kiyuni 28 1–28
章节.Kini 58:
To replace the two-engine Kini 55 and Kini 56 used on Joban Line freight trains, the Kini 58, based on the Kiro 58, appeared in 1978. As a two-engine car it had no space below the floor, so it differed from the Kini 28 in having the water tank installed inside the rear end face.

Nos. 1 and 2 were converted at Nagoya Works and No. 3 at Hata Works in 1978, and they were concentrated at Mito Engine Depot. On the Joban Line, an electrified route with dense train services, insufficient output and acceleration with a single DMH17-series engine was a problem, so two-engine cars were demanded. The Kini 55 was operated in common with the Kini 58 and was scrapped after the 1 February 1984 JNR timetable revision.

All cars were scrapped by February 1987 due to the abolition of freight transport.

Kiro 58 7, 8, 6 → Kini 58 1–3
章节.Kiha 28 cars demoted from the Kiro 28:
At the October 1980 timetable revision, Green cars were abolished on limited expresses within Shikoku and demoted to ordinary reserved cars, so the following conversions were carried out on Kiro 28s at Tadotsu Works.

• Demotion procedures by renumbering.
• The corridor carpet and armrest covers were removed, and seat covers changed from linen to vinyl.
• As differences in air-conditioning power equipment arose later, and similar conversions were also carried out in the Kyushu district, fine sub-series distinctions exist.
章节.Kiha 28 5000 series:
Cars with 4DQ power equipment. Six cars were converted to 4VK power equipment between 1980 and 1982 and renumbered to the 5200 series described below. Remaining cars were all scrapped in 1986.

Kiro 28 4, 15–17, 22, 25, 68, 69, 71, 110, 143, 144, 155, 157, 178–180, 202 → Kiha 28 5001–5018
章节.Kiha 28 5200 series:
The conversion content was the same as the 5000 series, but the difference was the distinction by 4VK power equipment. The cars are divided into four groups by number.

5201–5203: Shikoku district cars converted at the same time as the 5000 series.
Kiro 28 2177, 2194, 2195 → Kiha 28 5201–5203

5204–5209: The group converted from the 5000 series' 4DQ power equipment to 4VK.
Kiha 28 5017, 5016, 5013, 5018, 5015, 5014 → Kiha 28 5204–5209

5210–5220: The group made from Kiro 28 2000-series cars transferred to the Shikoku district from other regions between 1984 and 1985.
Kiro 28 2159, 2171, 2183, 2189, 2203, 2204, 2306, 2310, 2311, 2201, 2516 → Kiha 28 5210–5220

5221–5223: Kyushu district cars converted at Kokura Works.
Kiro 28 2151, 2152, 2192 → Kiha 28 5221–5223

Apart from the scrapping of six cars — 5201–5203, 5205, 5206 and 5208 — in the Shikoku district just before the privatization and breakup, each was inherited by the relevant regional JR, and they were scrapped by 1990 in the Shikoku district and by 1999 in the Kyushu district.
章节.Kiha 28 5300 series: Cars demoted from Kiroha 28 1. The Green room was converted in the same way as the 5000 and 5200 series and used as ordinary reserved seats, and the ordinary room was operated as non-reserved seats. Scrapped in 1984.
章节.Kiha 58 5000 series (JNR):
An accommodation-improved car converted at Kokura Works (present-day JR Kyushu Kokura General Rolling Stock Center) in the late JNR era in 1985, as reserved cars for limited expresses within Kyushu.

Seats were exchanged for reclining seats from scrapped Kiro 28 and Saha 481 parts.

Seat pitch was 1,150 mm, as for Green cars, so capacity became 52.

The window arrangement and seat pitch do not coincide.

All cars were inherited by JR Kyushu at the privatization and breakup. 5001 and 5004 were given engine replacements in 1989.

With the upgrading of the limited expresses "Yufu" and "Hinoyama" to super expresses, all cars except 5001 and 5004 were converted to "Seaside Liner", but all were scrapped by 2002 due to aging. There were also cars given the same conversion as the 5000 series without changing their numbers, and 5001 and 5002 duplicated numbers with JR Central.

Kiha 58 557, 558, 605, 757, 767, 1017, 1018 → Kiha 58 5001–5007
章节.Kiha 53 200 series:
From the late JNR era in 1986 to after JR privatization in 1988, five Kiha 58s were converted to double-cab cars and incorporated into the Kiha 53 type. The conversion was carried out by cutting off the rear of the body and attaching a scrapped cab; the exterior resembles the Kiha 58003 transferred from Fuji Kyuko to the Arita Railway, but the window arrangement differs. The type was designated Kiha 53, which already existed on the Kiha 45 series, and a new sub-series was created to avoid duplication with existing cars. For a conversion of the same intent, there is the Kiha 53 500 series converted from the Kiha 56; see the Kiha 53 500 series (501–510).

To improve operational efficiency on the Rikuu East Line, which runs through snowy areas on gradients, the double-cab Kiha 53 200 series appeared in 1987. Two non-air-conditioned Kiha 58s were converted at Tsuchizaki Works (present-day Akita General Rolling Stock Center), with a toilet installed in the saloon. They were allocated to Kogota Transport District and operated on the Rikuu East Line and elsewhere, then transferred to Aizu-Wakamatsu Transport District. They were operated on the Tadami Line and scrapped in 2000.

Kiha 58 741, 742 → Kiha 53 201, 202
章节.Fitting of music sirens:
As a level-crossing accident countermeasure, music sirens (special warning devices) were fitted as horns on twelve Kiha 58s in the Shikoku district between 1963 and 1965. The horn sound was an electronic tone of the scale "do-so-mi-do-do-so-mi-so-do", sounded at 7.5-second intervals, with speakers installed below the couplers. In fiscal 1964, two "whiskers", as on limited-express diesel railcars, were fitted to the front for identification purposes, making the cars easier to place at the head of formations.

The music sirens were later removed and the front end returned to the conventional specification. In 2008, just before JR Shikoku ended Kiha 58 series operation, "whiskers" were reproduced on Kiha 58 293.
章节.Fitting of Joban radio antennas:
Following the triple collision at Mikawashima Station on the Joban Line in May 1962 (the Mikawashima accident), train radio was to be installed on cars operated on the Joban Line from fiscal 1964 onward. This was carried out on the Kiha 58 series too, with two radio antennas fitted on the roof.

Cars air-conditioned after the fitting of the Joban radio antennas had unequally spaced air-conditioning units because of the equipment layout. Some air-conditioned cars transferred in from other lines did not have Joban radio antennas added, and as train radio spread nationwide in the late JNR era, the Joban radio antennas were progressively removed.
章节.Bogie exchange with the Kiha 81 series:
Of the Kiha 80 series, the Kiha 81 series built initially had a different brake system from the later Kiha 82 series, so work was carried out in fiscal 1969 to exchange the Kiha 81 series' bogies for the DT31B and TR68A, the same as the Kiha 82 series. The air-sprung DT27 and TR67 bogies released from the Kiha 81 series were transferred to the Kiha 58 series, being applied to 26 cars (some accounts say 24) of the Kiha 56 and 58 series. The DT22-series bogies released from the Kiha 58 series were transferred to exchange the Kiha 10 series' DT19-series bogies.

Conversions have been confirmed at least on Kiro 26 101; Kiro 28 81, 169, 503, 2112, 2125 and 2128; Kiha 28 2426; and Kiha 58 87, 100 and 269, but some cars, such as Kiro 26 101 and Kiro 28 2128, were later returned to the conventional DT22 series.
章节.Front reinforcement work:
To protect crew in the event of level-crossing accidents, conversions to reinforce the front of leading cars were carried out from fiscal 1975, and were started on the Kiha 58 series. On the Kiha 58 series, 4.5 mm steel plates were layered on the front waist panel; externally the thickness increased slightly, but there was no major change.

At JR East after privatization, front reinforcement work was actively promoted following the Narita Line Osuge level-crossing accident in 1991, and this series was also targeted. The work content differed by period and works, with examples where iron plates were used where stainless-steel reinforcement was applied elsewhere, and differences in whether anti-climbers were fitted.
章节.Niigata Railway Administration air-horn:
A conversion applied to cars allocated within the jurisdiction of the Niigata Railway Administration, a heavy-snow area. A cylindrical cover was fitted to the air horn (typhon) to prevent snow from entering.

Fitted cars included Kiha 58 1022 + Kiha 28 2371, operated to the very last at Niitsu Transport District even after JR East inheritance, and, in cases where they were used as they were even after transfer to other districts, Kiha 58 75, allocated to Morioka Rolling Stock Center, and Kiha 28 2010, stored at Akita General Rolling Stock Center.
章节.\"Notoji\" Romance Car conversion:
To promote tourism and improve the image of the Noto region, work was carried out in 1980 on Kiha 28 2049 at Nanao Engine Depot (present-day Nanao Railway Department), used on the limited express "Notoji" on the Nanao Line: exchanging the seats and installing sightseeing-guide videos.

Carpet was laid on the floor and the seats exchanged for rotating cross seats like those of the 0-series Shinkansen, changing capacity to 44.

To show sightseeing-guide videos in the car while running, video playback equipment was fitted, with 50-inch video screens at the front and rear of the saloon and 24 side speakers on the side walls.

One window near the rear of the saloon was made smaller, and a symbol mark was placed beside the vestibule window.

One AU13 air-conditioning unit was removed, leaving six.

This was an experimental conversion to promote tourism in the corridor region, and from 12 July that year it was operated as ordinary reserved-seat cars, one round trip in busy seasons only, under the Romance Car name. However, the exterior remained in the JNR limited-express color, making visual distinction difficult, and passenger numbers did not increase, so operation ended in 1982. The video playback equipment was later removed, and the car was also used on local trains. The car was converted to Kiro 29 552, an intermediate insert car of the Golden Express Astor, in 1987.
章节.Special preservation work: Entering the 1980s, limited-express diesel railcars, then 20 years from manufacture, began to show marked aging, but amid restraint on investment, special preservation work aimed at service improvement and safety was begun from fiscal 1981. The initial plan was for about 700 cars, with replacement of the lower body panels, rain gutters, toilets and washbasins.
章节.Conversions for \"Umineko\" and \"Murone:
On the Kita-Rias Line and Minami-Rias Line of the Sanriku Railway, which opened in 1984 as a third-sector railway, JNR cars were to make one round trip a day in the summer busy season, so accommodation conversions were carried out on the Kiha 58 series used on "Umineko" (Morioka–Miyako–Kuji) and "Murone" (Ichinoseki–Mori–Kamaishi).

Five cars were converted: Kiha 58 416, 486 and 1511, and Kiha 28 336 and 390. The livery was blue and ivory stripes representing the Sanriku sea and sky, and the seats were exchanged for rotating cross seats from scrapped 0-series Shinkansen cars.

Kiha 58 1511 and Kiha 28 390 were restored to conventional cross-seat ordinary cars, in line with engine replacement from fiscal 1989 after JR East inheritance, and the livery was changed to the Morioka color.
章节.Tatami-room conversions for the Nagasaki:
In 1985, the following conversions were carried out on two cars, Kiha 28 2006 and 2114, then allocated to Nagasaki Engine Depot.

• Carpet was laid on the floor, and karaoke and mahjong tables installed.
• White shoji screens were fitted to the side windows.
• An original head mark, "Batten NAGASAKI", was fitted at the front.

Revenue operation began on 26 May 1985. In operation, a Kiha 58 was coupled in the middle, and they were used on small group trains; both cars were scrapped in December 1986.
章节.Accommodation conversions for the Shikok: Accommodation-improvement conversions carried out at Tadotsu Works by the Shikoku District Bureau on surplus cars of this series generated by the reduction in limited-express operations in the late JNR era. Note that the conversions did not involve renumbering.
章节.Group-exclusive cars:
Between 1984 and 1985, conversions to the group-exclusive cars described below were carried out on three cars — Kiha 58 577 and 769, and Kiha 28 2475 — allocated to Takamatsu Driving Office.

• Seats and tables were exchanged for 0-series Shinkansen rotating cross seats, giving a capacity of 52.
• Karaoke equipment, speakers and a water dispenser were fitted.
• The exterior was changed to white with a blue wave pattern on one Kiha 58, and white with vermilion S-shaped lines on the other two cars.

They were used for group trains and as extra cars on limited expresses, but were demoted to ordinary cars in 1988 when "Tabidachi" and "Rainbow" appeared after JR privatization. On demotion, the exterior was changed to the JR Shikoku color, and the seats and tables were left unchanged, with only the karaoke equipment, speakers and water dispenser removed, and they were used on limited expresses like other ordinary cars.
章节.Grade-up conversions:
Conversions carried out between 1985 and 1986 on Kiha 58 1035 and Kiha 28 2476, allocated to Tokushima Diesel Car Depot (present-day Tokushima Driving Office).

• The livery was changed to white with vermilion S-shaped lines, as used for the group-exclusive cars described above.
• Kiha 58 1035's seats and tables were exchanged for 0-series Shinkansen rotating cross seats, and Kiha 28 2476's for Kiha 181-series rotating cross seats, giving a capacity of 60.

This conversion omitted the karaoke equipment and water dispenser of the group-exclusive cars and increased the seat capacity, premised on scheduled limited-express operation.

They were demoted to ordinary cars in 1988 when "Tabidachi" and "Rainbow" appeared after JR privatization. On demotion, the exterior was changed to the JR Shikoku color, and the seats and tables were left unchanged, and they were used like other ordinary cars. Kiha 28 2476 later had its toilet and washroom equipment removed and was semi-cross-seated in 1990.
章节.Fitting of skirts to flat-window cars: Late-built panoramic-window cars had skirts from new, but some flat-window cars allocated in Shikoku and Kyushu were also given skirt-fitting conversions as a level-crossing accident countermeasure.
章节.Major conversions after JR privatization: After privatization, each company carried out conversions and refurbishments specialized to its operations and the lines on which cars were deployed.
章节.JR East conversions: In addition to life extension through body refurbishment work and the special preservation work, many cars were semi-cross-seated to suit conditions on the lines where they were operated, but at JR East there were the following examples of major conversions without renumbering.
章节.Engine replacement and fire prevention m:
At JR East, on-road testing of engines to replace the DMH17 series had been carried out from January 1988, but during this, in March of the same year, the Joyful Train "Salon Express Arcadia" suffered a fire accident. The cause was overheating of the exhaust pipe. Also, as countermeasures considering the aging of the DMH17H engines themselves and fuel-consumption problems, from September 1989 engines were replaced on Kiha 58-series cars and other DMH17-series-equipped cars such as the Kiha 52 and Kiha 35 series, with Niigata Engineering (DMF13HZ), Komatsu (DMF11HZ (SA6D125-H-1)) and Cummins (DMF14HZ (NTA855-R1)) engines.

These new engines were originally rated at 330 PS or 350 PS, but when replaced on DMH17-series cars the output was reduced to 250 PS to cope with the capacity limits of the reused conventional liquid transmissions.
章节.Car refurbishment work: At JR East, car refurbishment work aimed at life extension began in 1990. The work included replacement of exterior panels, exchange of passenger doors and replacement of decorative panels, and seats were semi-cross-seated except in the Morioka area.
章节.\"Yoneshiro\" and \"Gassan\" grade-up ca: To improve service on premium trains such as the limited expresses "Yoneshiro" and "Gassan", Kiha 58-series grade-up cars appeared in fiscal 1991. In addition to the usual refurbishment work, seats were exchanged for reclining seats, and electric direction blinds were fitted for the side destination indicators.
章节.Conversion to training cars:
At JR East, cars called "training cars" appeared for the periodic education and training of crew in handling abnormal situations and emergency measures. They were applied to surplus 103-, 113-, 115-, 455- and 485-series electric cars, but for diesel railcars, Morioka Rolling Stock Center cars of this series were converted at Tsuchizaki Works, mainly internally, with the removal of some seats, the installation of lockers and tables for storing supplies, and monitors and racks for carrying videos for audiovisual training. Externally, two white lines and "training car" markings were added to distinguish them from ordinary cars.

After conversion they remained allocated to Morioka Rolling Stock Center and were always operated forming a unit with Kiha 58 75, but were scrapped in November 2008, eliminating the type.

(Kiha 28 102 →) Kiha 28 2102 → Kiya 28 1
章节.JR Central conversions: Conversions carried out by Nagoya Works on the Kiha 58s for "Kasuga" and "Mie". The reclining seats were parts from scrapped 0-series Tokaido Shinkansen cars. Unconverted Nagoya Rolling Stock District cars allocated to "Kasuga" and "Mie" were also later changed to the same color.
章节.Kiha 58 3000 series (for \"Kasuga\"):
In 1989, Kiha 58 5714 appeared, with the seats of Kiha 58 714 exchanged for reclining seats for the limited express "Kasuga". As a 5000-series speed-up car for the rapid "Mie" appeared in 1991, the former 5000 series was renumbered to the 3000 series. Scrapped in 2001.

Kiha 58 714 → Kiha 58 5714 → Kiha 58 3001
章节.Kiha 58 5000 and 5100 series (for \"Mie\:
At the March 1991 timetable revision, some "Mie" rapid trains were speeded up, and conversions were carried out on the Kiha 58 and 65 used on these trains for 110 km/h operation: replacement of engines, transmissions and bogies, and renewal of the accommodation. Three Kiha 58 cars received the following conversions.

• Engines replaced with Cummins C-DMF14HZ engines (350 PS / 2,000 rpm) and Niigata Converter transmissions.
• Bogies exchanged for DT31C air-sprung bogies from scrapped Kiha 82-series cars, for 110 km/h compatibility.
• Seats exchanged for reclining seats.

The 5100 series was a distinction because the donor cars were panoramic-window cars. After the appearance of the Kiha 75, they were used on special trains and on the Taketoyo Line, but were scrapped in 2001. Also, 5001 and 5002 duplicated numbers with JR Kyushu.

Kiha 58 680, 1033, 1101 → Kiha 58 5001, 5002, 5101
章节.JR West conversions: Although engine replacement was not carried out, many cars received life-extension work. Cars used on limited-express services on local lines such as "Notoji" and "Miyoshi" had their seats changed and liveries altered. Cars for local lines often received one-man-operation conversion work and semi-cross-seating.
章节.Life-extension N, NA and N40 work: The JNR-era special preservation work was continued at JR West as life-extension N work; from 1990, life-extension NA work was carried out on cars already given the special preservation work, aiming at further advanced life extension, and life-extension N40 work, anticipating 40 years of use after manufacture, was also carried out. These works included replacement of saloon decorative panels, renewal of toilets and washrooms, and renewal of wiring and piping.
章节.Kiroha 28 100 series:
The limited express "Sakyu" between Okayama and Tottori ran as a four-car formation including a Green car, but as the Green car's ridership was low, the Kiroha 28 100 series was converted at JR West's Tottori and Goto Works between 1987 and 1988, halving the Green car and making a three-car formation. The sub-series distinction of 100 was made to distinguish it from the Kiroha 28 0 series, which appeared in 1974 and was eliminated in 1980. The donor cars were all late-built model-change cars of the group with low gutter height.

A partition sliding door and wall were newly installed in the center of the saloon, and the rear side was changed to ordinary seats (box seats).

With the installation of the partition, the first window on the front side of the ordinary seats was made smaller and fixed. Thus, unlike the 0 series, the exterior also changed.

The ordinary-seat pitch was 1,605 mm.

The window arrangement and seat spacing do not coincide. Also, although scrapped parts were used for the seats, the Green seats were exchanged for an improved semi-bucket type.

Capacity was 28 Green seats and 40 ordinary seats.

Later, at the same time as the conversion of the Kiha 58 7200 series for "Sakyu" (see below), conversions were carried out, including exchanging the ordinary seats for Green-car rotating reclining seats and changing the livery, reducing the ordinary-seat capacity to 28.

Although not a 2000 series, as the donor cars were Kiro 28 2000 series, they continued to carry 4VK power equipment.

They were allocated to the Nishi-Tottori Rolling Stock Branch of Tottori Railway Department, but 101 and 102 were scrapped in 1998 following the abolition of "Sakyu" in November 1997. 103 and 104 transferred to Okayama Electric Car Depot Diesel Car Center (present-day Okayama Diesel Car District) and were used on the limited express "Tsuyama" between Okayama and Tsuyama, but were scrapped in 2004 due to aging.

Kiro 28 2508, 2509, 2517, 2518 → Kiroha 28 101–104
章节.Kiha 53 1000 series:
For single-car operation of Nanao Line local trains, three air-conditioned Kiha 58s were converted to double-cab cars between 1987 and 1988 and incorporated into the Kiha 53 type. They have no toilet. Although air-conditioning units are carried on the roof, as air-conditioning power equipment is not carried, they cannot use the air conditioning alone. Except for the air conditioning, they are the cars closest in appearance to the Arita Railway Kiha 58003.

The conversions were carried out at Mattō Works (present-day Kanazawa General Rolling Stock Office). They were allocated to Nanao Driving Office (present-day Nanao Railway Department), and after the electrification of the Nanao Line in 1991 transferred to Toyama Railway Department and were operated on the Takayama Main Line. In 1996, with the replacement by Kiha 120s on the Takayama Main Line, they transferred to Takaoka Railway Department and were operated on the Johana Line, Himi Line and elsewhere. All were scrapped in 2005, eliminating the sub-series.

Kiha 58 683, 752, 783 → Kiha 53 1001–1003
章节.6000 series (for \"Takayama\"):
To improve service on the limited express "Takayama", the 6000 series with accommodation improvements appeared in 1990–91. The engines remained the conventional DMH17H, the bogies the conventional DT22/TR51-series metal-spring bogies, and the maximum speed was unchanged at 95 km/h. The conversion was carried out at Tottori Works.

• Ordinary-car seats were exchanged for reclining seats.
• Capacity was changed to 64.
• Electric heating.
• Repainting to a dedicated livery.

With the abolition of "Takayama" at the December 1999 timetable revision, all cars were scrapped in 2000.

Kiha 58 1028, 1050, 1052 → Kiha 58 6001–6003
Kiha 28 3007, 3008 → Kiha 28 6001, 6002
Kiro 28 2510, 2162 → Kiro 28 6001, 6002
章节.One-man operation conversions (JR West):
To rationalize local-line operation, one-man conversions of Kiha 58-series cars operated on the Johana, Himi, Obama and Maizuru Lines and the Kansai Main Line were carried out between 1989 and 1992. The conversions included the installation of one-man equipment such as fare tables and ticket-issuing machines, and longitudinal seating near the doors; except on the Kansai Main Line, the areas near the front and rear passenger doors were longitudinal-seated, while for the Kansai Main Line only the front door near the cab was longitudinal-seated.

The number of cars converted was 15 — eight Kiha 58 and seven Kiha 28 — for the Kansai Main Line, and 39 — 18 Kiha 58, 18 Kiha 28 and 3 Kiha 53 — for the Maizuru, Obama, Johana and Himi Lines.
章节.5500 series (long-seat cars):
With the electrification of the Nanao Line in 1991, Kiha 58-series cars on that line became surplus, and were used for replacement accompanying the complete abolition of passenger-car trains on the Bantan Line at the March 1992 timetable revision. For transfer to local trains on the Bantan Line and the Kishin Line, longitudinal-seat conversions were carried out with commuter transport in mind, and the Kiha 58 5500 series and Kiha 28 5500 series appeared in 1991–92. Replacement of the floor covering and the addition of more straps were also carried out. The conversions were carried out at Tottori and Mattō Works.

All cars were allocated to Himeji Railway Department, but all were scrapped in 1999, eliminating the sub-series. After scrapping, 20 of the 31 cars were transferred to Thailand.

Kiha 58 200, 264, 289, 311, 401, 407, 408, 428–430, 433, 538, 559, 679, 682, 751 → Kiha 58 5501–5516
Kiha 28 2048, 2068, 2085, 2088, 2091, 2096, 2128, 2163, 2166, 2169, 2177, 2317, 2322, 2327, 2331 → Kiha 28 5501–5515
章节.Kiha 58 7200 series (for \"Tango\" and \:
To improve service and the image of the limited expresses "Tango" and "Sakyu", the Kiha 58 7200 series, with accommodation conversions and life-extension work, appeared in fiscal 1991–92. The engines remained the conventional DMH17H, the bogies the conventional DT22/TR51-series metal-spring bogies, and the maximum speed was unchanged at 95 km/h (85 km/h for "Sakyu" cars). The conversion was carried out at Goto Works.

• Seats were exchanged for reclining seats from scrapped 0-series Shinkansen cars.
• Toilets and washrooms were renewed.
• Only "Sakyu" cars were repainted to white and light-blue-based colors.

All cars of this sub-series were scrapped by 2005 due to the abolition of the relevant trains and aging.

Kiha 58 78, 690, 467, 696, 259, 451, 553, 625, 638, 668, 669, 749 → Kiha 58 7201–7212
章节.Kiha 58 7300 series (for \"Edel Kita-Kin:
Converted at Goto Works in 1991 as a spare car for the limited express "Edel Kita-Kinki". Although a limited-express car, the engines remained the conventional DMH17H, the bogies the conventional DT22/TR51-series metal-spring bogies, and the maximum speed was unchanged at 95 km/h. Allocated to Fukuchiyama Driving Office, later transferring to Toyooka Railway Department. Scrapped in 2000.

Kiha 58 686 → Kiha 58 7301
章节.JR Shikoku conversions: Accommodation improvements had been carried out since the JNR-era Shikoku District Bureau, but after the privatization and breakup, cars for limited-express service had their liveries changed to the JR Shikoku color from 1988, and floor materials, partition doors, wall panels and luggage racks exchanged, and, except for the Kiha 28 5000 and 5200 series, seats were bucket-seated. In addition, some Kiha 58 cars were grade-upped, with their seats exchanged for rotating cross seats generated by the reclining-seating of Kiha 181-series cars, and capacity changed to 60.
章节.JR Kyushu conversions:
Limited-express cars had their seats changed to reclining seats and floorboards replaced, and local-train cars received suburban interior conversion work, but conversions involving renumbering were limited to the Joyful Trains described below, classified as the 7000 and 8000 series. In addition, conversions reusing only the bogies and machinery of two Kiha 58s for the Kiha 70, intermediate cars of the Kiha 71 series for "Yufuin no Mori (I)", were carried out in 1989 and 1990.

Kiha 58 490, 436 → Kiha 70 1, 2
章节.Conversions to Joyful Trains and sightse:
This series had many crew and maintenance staff familiar with its handling, and by the 1980s many cars had air conditioning. Moreover, as diesel railcars, there were few constraints on operating sections and train length, making them suitable for conversions dedicated to group trains. Making use of these characteristics, group-exclusive cars converted from this series began to appear in various places from the late JNR era, and many Joyful Trains converted from this series, with salon-style interiors and tatami saloons, appeared at the JR companies after privatization, being operated in various forms as a revenue-increasing measure.

However, with changes in travel styles and economic downturns, and as even the last-built cars of this series were 18 years old at the time of JNR privatization in 1987, the overall age of the fleet became high, and conversion targets for Joyful Trains also shifted to the Kiha 40 series, which was newer than this series, so from the late 1990s many cars were scrapped due to aging. In this series, JR East Morioka Division's "Kenji" was scrapped in September 2018, and as of 2019 no cars remained in the JR Group as this series.

Some cars converted to Joyful Trains had their types changed from Kiha 56 and Kiha 58 to Kiro 59, Kiha 59, Kiha 27 and Kiha 28 to Kiro 29 and Kiha 29, and the Kisaro 59 — the only trailer car in the broad this series — was completed in this group. The Kisaro 59 was a car transferred from Type 12 passenger cars.
章节.\"Komachi\" → \"Obako\":
A tatami diesel railcar converted in 1984 for the JNR-era Akita Railway Administration, to meet demand for tourist areas and hot-spring resorts in the Tohoku region. After JR East inheritance it belonged to the Akita Division. In 1997 it was renamed "Obako" to cede the name "Komachi" to the Akita Shinkansen. It became an ordinary car in 2001, was laid up from 2004, and was scrapped in 2006.

Kiha 58 622 + Kiha 28 2389 + Kiha 58 759 → Kiro 59 501 + Kiro 29 501 + Kiro 59 502 → Kiha 59 501 + Kiha 29 501 + Kiha 59 502
章节.\"Elegance Akkie\":
As the Akita Railway Administration's tatami diesel railcar was well received, it was converted in 1985 into a Western-style diesel railcar aimed at younger people. Like "Obako", it belonged to the JNR-era Akita Railway Administration → JR East Akita Division. Scrapped in 1997.

Kiha 58 1517 + Kiha 28 2408 + Kiha 58 1532 → Kiro 59 503 + Kiro 29 502 + Kiro 59 504
章节.Carpet cars (Niigata area):
Carpet diesel railcars (no train name) for the Niigata Railway Administration (later JR East Niigata Division); three Kiha 58 cars and one Kiha 28 were converted in 1985.

Kiha 58: 120, 446, 1021
Kiha 28: 2032
章节.\"Salon Express Arcadia\":
A European-style diesel railcar for the Niigata area, converted in 1987 before the privatization and breakup of JNR; three cars appeared: two Kiro 59 and one Kiro 29. The front of the Kiro 59 had an observation lounge in a style following the Hokkaido-oriented "Resort Express". The conversion was carried out at Niitsu Rolling Stock Works (→ Niitsu Rolling Stock Manufacturing Works → present-day General Rolling Stock Manufacturing Works Niitsu Office), owned by the Niigata Division.

In 1988, Kiro 59 508 was completely burned out from a fire caused by overheating of the exhaust pipe while running on the Joetsu Line, and was scrapped. The remaining two cars were laid up and later re-converted into the "Kenji" described below.

Kiha 58 626 + Kiha 28 2010 + Kiha 58 650 → Kiro 59 508 + Kiro 29 505 + Kiro 59 509
章节.\"Edelweiss\":
A European-style diesel railcar for the Morioka area; two Kiha 58 cars and one Kiha 28 were converted in 1988. Tsuchizaki Works (present-day Akita General Rolling Stock Center) carried out the conversion. It was owned by the Morioka Division and scrapped in 2002.

Kiha 58 619 + Kiha 28 2509 + Kiha 58 744
章节.\"Gracia\" → \"Kogane\":
A European-style diesel railcar for the Sendai area; two Kiro 59 and one Kiro 29 appeared as "Gracia" in 1989. Owned by the Sendai Division; converted at Koriyama Works (present-day Koriyama General Rolling Stock Center). It was changed to an ordinary car in 2000, then renovated as "Kogane" in 2003. It withdrew from service on 26 December 2010 due to aging, and was later exported to the Philippines.

Kiha 58 1038 + Kiha 28 2505 + Kiha 58 1039 → Kiro 59 510 + Kiro 29 506 + Kiro 59 511 → Kiha 59 510 + Kiha 29 506 + Kiha 59 511
章节.\"Kenji\":
As a spectator-transport train for the 1992 Sanriku and Sea Exposition, two Kiha 58 cars and one Kiha 28 were converted in 1992. With the total-loss scrapping of Kiro 59 508, Kiro 29 505 + Kiro 59 509, which had been laid up, were transferred to the Morioka Division, and, including Kiha 58 1505, needed as a replacement leading car, the conversion was carried out at Tsuchizaki Works in 1992. At the same time, they were also converted to ordinary cars, so Kiro 29 505 + Kiro 59 509 reverted to their original numbers.

During the exposition they ran as the "Sanriku Marine Liner", and after it ended they were operated as "Kenji" on group and special trains. After JR West's Kiha 58 series ended operation in 2011, they were the last cars operated in revenue service as the Kiha 58 series anywhere in the JR Group, but operation ended with a group special train on 8 September 2018, and they were scrapped on 26 September of that year.

Kiha 58 1505 + Kiro 29 505 + Kiro 59 509 → Kiha 58 1505 + Kiha 28 2010 + Kiha 58 650
章节.\"Fureai SUN-IN\":
A tatami diesel railcar for the Yonago area; two Kiro 59 and one Kiro 29 were converted, completed in fiscal 1985.

Kiha 58 1123 + Kiha 28 3006 + Kiha 58 1126 → Kiro 59 505 + Kiro 29 503 + Kiro 59 506
章节.\"Fureai Paru\":
A two-car tatami diesel railcar, designed with small groups in mind and flexibility in entering lines; one Kiro 59 and one Kiro 29 were completed in fiscal 1985. The front was made non-through, with a large window from the assistant driver's seat over the former gangway.

Kiha 58 1134 + Kiha 28 2431 → Kiro 59 507 + Kiro 29 504
章节.\"Honobono SUN-IN\":
An additional tatami car for the Yonago area; two cars, Kiro 59 551 and Kiro 29 551, were converted and completed in fiscal 1987. The interior has a Western room at the car end near the cab, and a tatami-floored Japanese room elsewhere.

Kiha 58 1129 + Kiha 28 2453 → Kiro 59 551 + Kiro 29 551
章节.\"Golden Express Astor\":
"Yūtopia", converted from the Kiha 65 series in fiscal 1986, was used on the holiday limited express "Yūtopia Wakura", so cars were to be added to enable group special trains to run on holidays as well. Appearing in fiscal 1987 as a new group-use car based on "Yūtopia" was the "Golden Express Astor": the two leading cars were converted from Kiha 65 to Kiro 65, and the intermediate car from Kiha 28 to Kiro 28.

At the 1997 refurbishment work, Kiro 29 554 was converted as a replacement for Kiro 29 552 due to aging. Also, the Kiro 65 551 + 1551 at both ends could operate in multiple with 485-series electric cars, but as the Kiro 29's maximum speed was limited to 95 km/h, multiple-unit operation was not possible when it was inserted.

Kiha 28 2049 → Kiro 29 552 (converted 1987 → scrapped 1997)
Kiro 28 2511 → Kiro 29 554 (converted 1997 → scrapped 2006)
章节.\"Resort Saloon Festa\":
For the Hiroshima Division, Kiro 59 552, 553 and Kiro 29 553 were completed in fiscal 1988 as a European-style diesel railcar. The front had a unique design modeled on a fish's face, with an LED display and speakers installed inside the movable lips.

Kiha 58 295 + Kiha 28 2056 + Kiha 58 135 → Kiro 59 552 + Kiro 29 553 + Kiro 59 553
章节.\"Viva West\":
An event diesel railcar based in Yamaguchi Prefecture; two cars, Kiha 59 and Kiha 29 501, were converted in fiscal 1989. The front was a non-through type with a slant for a smart image and sense of speed, and the sides were structured to look like continuous windows.

Kiha 58 176 + Kiha 28 2132 → Kiha 59 501 + Kiha 29 501
章节.\"Seychelles\":
To eliminate the coupling of passenger trains with the Suha 12 701 "Ikoi", a Type 12 group-use conversion car at the Fukuchiyama area, two Kiha 58-series cars and the Suha 12 701 were converted in fiscal 1989. The leading car was a Kiro 59 converted from a Kiha 58, and the intermediate car the Kisaro 59 converted from the Type 12 Suha 12.

Kiha 58 1111 + (Suha 12 5 → Suha 12 701) + Kiha 58 1119 → Kiro 59 554 + Kisaro 59 501 + Kiro 59 555
章节.\"Tabidachi\":
Converted in 1988 as group trains for school excursions and similar, in time for the opening of the Seto Ohashi Bridge. The design adopted white with blue and green bands, JR Shikoku's corporate colors.

The interior had floor materials, partition doors, wall panels and luggage racks exchanged, and the seats renewed to bucket-type cross seats with large folding tables. Capacity was 84, but Kiha 58 306 was 76, as it had a chaperone room fitted with a car telephone.

Kiha 58: 305, 306
Kiha 28: 2153, 2432
章节.\"Rainbow\":
Converted in 1988 at the same time as the aforementioned "Tabidachi", but as a general-group diesel railcar. The design adopted white with blue and pink bands, JR Shikoku's corporate colors.

As well as floor materials, partition doors, wall panels and luggage racks, the seats were exchanged for reclining seats with tables. Each car had karaoke equipment with display monitors and a lounge installed, changing capacity to 52. Also, one side window was filled in to install the display monitors.

Including "Tabidachi", group and special-train operation to the Honshu area was considered from the planning stage, so they were the only diesel railcars then belonging to JR Shikoku, excluding its limited-express types, fitted with train radios compatible with the Honshu area.

Kiha 58: 464, 649
Kiha 28: 2490, 2491
章节.Cycle trains:
Converted for the "Cycle Trains" operated on the Yodo Line in July–August 1999. Bicycle illustrations were painted on the sides, the seats were removed, and bicycle securing fittings were installed in the car. Passengers rode in the coupled Kiha 32.

Kiha 58: 770
章节.\"Rakuda\":
To attract group customers in southern Kyushu, six cars — three Kiha 58 and three Kiha 28 — with accommodation conversions appeared between fiscal 1983 and 1986. Seats became rotating cross seats from scrapped limited-express electric cars, and group-oriented equipment such as karaoke machines was added.

Kiha 58 140 + Kiha 28 2436 (converted 1983)
Kiha 58 190 + Kiha 28 2420 (converted 1984)

章节.\"Kitchomu\" → \"Joyful Train Oita\":
As an event car for the Oita area, two cars, Kiha 28 2487 and Kiha 58 190, were converted to "Kitchomu" (kitchomu) in fiscal 1985. Kiha 58 190 was a re-conversion from "Rakuda". The interior: the Kiha 58 was fully tatami-floored, while the Kiha 28 had reclining seats from scrapped Kiro 28s in the cab-side half and tatami flooring in the rear half.

As a group-use car for the Kumamoto area, one Kiha 28, two Kiha 58 and one Kiha 65 were converted in 1986. Seats were changed to reclining seats from scrapped Kiro 28s, and karaoke and audio equipment were also provided. By 1994 they had been re-converted to the "Huis Ten Bosch Shuttle" and "Seaside Liner".
