章节.\"Yūtopia\":
To upgrade group transport, "Rakuda" formation 1 was re-converted in 1987 and "Yūtopia" appeared. The front had a large assistant-driver window similar to the Hiroshima area's "Fureai Paru", and the passenger door immediately behind the cab was removed from the sides, with a large window on the assistant-driver side and audio equipment on the cab side.

Kiha 58 140 + Kiha 28 2436
章节.\"Bun-Bun\":
A tatami car for small-group transport in the Kyushu district; two cars, Kiha 58 and Kiha 28 8001, appeared in fiscal 1986. The interior had sunken kotatsu tables arranged, and horizontal shoji screens fitted at the side windows.

Kiha 58 689 + Kiha 28 2489 → Kiha 58 8001 + Kiha 28 8001
章节.\"Saloon Express\":
As a sightseeing train for the Kumamoto area, one Kiha 58 and one Kiha 65 were converted in fiscal 1987. The gangway diaphragm frame was removed, the coupling attachment was made flush with the body, and a head mark was fitted to the gangway door. The side windows were fixed, and the floor of the seat area was raised 200 mm, with one- and two-person cross seats arranged.

Kiha 58 1141 + (Kiha 65 502) → Kiha 58 7001 + (Kiha 65 7001)
章节.\"Joyful Train Nagasaki\":
As an event train for the Nagasaki area, Kiha 58/65 7002 appeared in fiscal 1988. The interior has a lounge in the cab-side half and general seats in the rear half.

It later transferred to the Kumamoto area, becoming "Joyful Train Kumamoto".

Kiha 58 298 + (Kiha 65 12) → Kiha 58 7002 + (Kiha 65 7002)
章节.\"Aqua Express\":
To expand demand and improve the image of the Kashii Line, which has tourist spots such as Umi-no-Nakamichi along it, Kiha 58 7003 and 7004 and Kiha 28 7001 appeared in fiscal 1988. The fronts of Kiha 58 7004 and Kiha 28 7001 were converted to non-through structures with a receding angle, while Kiha 58 7003 was the same as conventional cars. The side windows were fixed, and a sunroof of curved glass was also provided.

Kiha 28 2445 + Kiha 58 702 + Kiha 58 723 → Kiha 28 7001 + Kiha 58 7003 + Kiha 58 7004
章节.\"Fureai GO\":
A Japanese-style diesel railcar for the northern Kyushu area; Kiha 58 8002 and Kiha 65 8001 appeared in fiscal 1988. The interior was a blend of Japanese and Western styles, with carpeted floors and horizontal shoji screens fitted at the windows.

Kiha 58 57 + (Kiha 65 55) → Kiha 58 8002 + (Kiha 65 8001)
章节.\"Shiranui\":
As a renewal of the conventional Japanese-style diesel railcars, Kiha 58 190 of the former "Joyful Train Oita" and Kiha 28 2436 of the former "Yūtopia" were re-converted in fiscal 1993 and "Shiranui" appeared. The conversion involved re-tatami and shoji, and renewal of the toilet and washroom.

Soon after its appearance, JR Kyushu abolished most of its Joyful Trains, and "Shiranui" operated for only about ten months.

Kiha 58 190 + Kiha 28 2436
章节.\"TORO-Q\":
To mark the 2002 "Torokko Train Summit", three Tora 70000-series open cars and Kiha 58 569 and Kiha 65 36 appeared as "TORO-Q". Belonging to Oita Rolling Stock Center of the Oita Railway Business Department, they were formed with Kiha 65 36 and Tora 70000 cars and operated between Yufuin, Minami-Yufu and Oita on the Kyudai Main Line, but operation ended on 29 November 2009.

Thereafter they were restored to JNR colors together with Kiha 65 36, and were used mainly on the "Revival! Limited Express Series" and similar until the vehicle's inspection expiry in August 2010, withdrawing from service after the revival limited express "Hikari Final" on 29 August.

After withdrawal, exhibitions continued from the "Train Festa" held at Oita Rolling Stock Center on 23 October 2010, and after a final photo event at Oita Rolling Stock Center on 2 June 2013, they were transferred to Kokura General Rolling Stock Center on 5 June of that month, and scrapped on 16 March 2015.

Kiha 58 569 + (Tora 70000-series open wagons x3 + Kiha 65 36)
章节.\"Aso 1962\":
Following the withdrawal of the steam-hauled train "SL Aso BOY", whose locomotive, 8620 class No. 58654, was scrapped due to aging, two cars, Kiha 58 139 and Kiha 28 2401, were converted in 2005 as a new Aso-area sightseeing train. They retired on 26 December 2010. They were the last Kiha 58-series cars to remain at JR Kyushu, but were scrapped in January 2019.

Kiha 58 139 + Kiha 28 2401
章节.Multiple-unit operation of electric and:
In 1964 (Showa 39), a test of multiple-unit operation of electric and diesel railcars — a technical issue on the Joban Line — was carried out. The necessary main equipment was fitted, and couplers and gangway diaphragms for both electric cars and diesel railcars were modified (as in the original), and the test was conducted with a formation of eight 451-series cars and three Kiha 28 cars (plus two cars as dead weight). There were deemed to be no obstacles in practical terms, but as there were issues with crew operation and instructor training for electric and diesel railcars, and cars required conversion, the benefits of multiple-unit operation were deemed thin.

Next, in December 1966 (Showa 41), a multiple-unit test between the 165 series and the Kiha 58 was carried out between Tsuruta and Nikko on the Nikko Line. Coordinated-operation conversions were carried out on Kuha 165 and the Kiha 58, and the Kiha 58 was fitted with a brake changeover device. The test confirmed that coordinated operation of electric and diesel railcars was possible.
章节.JR East's comparative test of refurbishm:
At JR East, to select refurbishment engines to replace the DMH17 series, a long-term test was carried out between January and November 1988, with engines replaced on three Morioka Passenger Car Depot Kiha 58s. The targets were Kiha 58 614, 277 and 628, with two each of Cummins NTA855R1 on Kiha 58 614, Niigata Engineering DMF13HZ on Kiha 58 277, and Komatsu SA6D125H1 installed on each car. Engine output was set at 330 PS in all cases.

The test was carried out on the Kamaishi Line, Hanawa Line and elsewhere, and based on the results, full engine replacement was carried out on the Kiha 58 series, Kiha 52 and others. After the test, all three test cars were standardized on the DMF13HZ. During this test period, in March 1988, the Joyful Train "Salon Express Arcadia" fire accident occurred.
章节.Introduction to premium trains:
In April 1961 the Kiha 56 series began revenue operation on the Nemuro Main Line's "Karigachi", in July the Kiha 57 series on the Shin'etsu Main Line's "Shiga", and in October the Kiha 58 series on the Chuo East Line and Oito Line's "Alps", in each case as limited-express trains.

Thereafter, the Kiha 56 and 58 series continued to be built in large quantities of 100–200 cars per year, and from their introduction until scrapping they were deployed in large numbers on trains in non-electrified sections throughout Japan, except Shizuoka Prefecture (although some cars were allocated to Numazu Engine Depot at delivery, they never actually entered service there and transferred after a very short period).

In the Boso area, where special timetables are arranged in summer for beachgoers, and in the Hokkaido area, busy in peak season, large numbers of extra and special trains are run, so this series was characterized by many formally allocated cars from new builds and transfers, in addition to cars borrowed from other regions. Many of these cars belonged to the relevant area's vehicle base for only the two to three summer months, transferring to other regions after the season ended.

New builds continued until fiscal 1969, in line with the JNR Modernization Five-Year Plan, and thereafter, for about 20 years from the 1970s, they were widely used on limited-express trains on trunk and sub-trunk lines, and on local trains at the ends of lines. However, with the advance of trunk-line electrification and the upgrading of limited-express trains to super expresses, diesel-railcar limited expresses gradually narrowed their sphere of operation. This series contributed greatly to the air conditioning of trains in regional districts in the 1970s, but entering the 1990s it became something of a presence left behind by the trends of the times in terms of in-car equipment. Its maximum speed was 95 km/h, which was sufficient for the many lines run by limited-express trains, including trunk lines.

Green cars began to become surplus in the mid-1970s, and the first scrapping occurred at the 10 March 1975 timetable revision. Some were converted to baggage cars and postal-baggage cars, and in the Shikoku district they were demoted to ordinary reserved cars at the 1 October 1980 timetable revision. At privatization, 21 Kiro 28s were inherited in total — seven by JR Central and 14 by JR West — of which 20 were final-batch cars of the 2300 and 2500 series with 4VK air-conditioning power equipment, and only 2162 from the long-formation 100 series. All 0-series cars were scrapped or converted to other types in the JNR era.

On the other hand, even into the 1980s there were still many multi-level trains performing complex divisions and couplings, and although reduced from their peak, limited-express trains with this series were still operated.

Limited expresses remained that ran entirely on electrified sections for reasons of vehicle supply and operations, such as "Shirayuki" between Kanazawa and Aomori, "Oga" between Ueno and Akita via the Ou Main Line, and "Akakura" between Nagoya and Niigata via the Chuo West Line, Shinonoi Line and Shin'etsu Main Line.

At the 15 November 1982 JNR timetable revision, accompanying the opening of the Tohoku and Joetsu Shinkansen, the many limited expresses in the Tohoku and Joetsu-Shin'etsu areas to which this series had been deployed became subject to rationalization: upgrades to super expresses, frequency reductions and abolition.

At the 14 March 1985 JNR timetable revision, Green cars were abolished in the Kyushu district, and many limited expresses were again upgraded to super expresses or downgraded to rapid trains, so a large number of surplus cars were generated compared with before, with the following tendencies.

• Transfer to local-train operation (see below).
• Use as donor cars for Joyful Train conversions.
• Cars continuing on limited-express and rapid service were given accommodation improvements, with seats exchanged for rotating cross seats or reclining seats.

Separately, to provide access to the site of the science exposition (Expo '85) held from 17 March to 16 September 1985, the temporary rapid "Expo Liner" was operated on the Joban Line, using surplus cars of this series from Mito Engine Depot that had been on the limited expresses "Tokiwa" and "Okukuji", abolished at the timetable revision three days before the opening.

Thereafter, from the 1990s to the early 2000s, nearly all diesel-railcar limited-express trains across the country disappeared, being abolished or upgraded to super expresses. The last scheduled limited express using this series was "Miyoshi" on the JR West Geibi Line, but it was abolished at the 1 July 2007 timetable revision.
章节.Transfer to local and other trains:
Although becoming surplus as a limited-express type, even in 1980 the earliest cars were less than 20 years old and had ample service life remaining. Some had already been used on local trains, mainly non-air-conditioned cars, but from the 1980s air-conditioned cars were also transferred in large numbers, being used to replace the aged, non-air-conditioned Kiha 20 and Kiha 55 series.

At the time, the Kiha 40 series, built to replace the aged Kiha 10 series, was unsuitable for gradient sections due to the compatibility of engine output and transmission settings and car-weight problems, whereas this series, being mainly two-engine cars, was easy to deploy on gradient sections, and, particularly west of the Chubu region, with many air-conditioned cars from limited-express use, maintained a reasonable standard of equipment, contributing greatly to the air conditioning of regional trains.

Cars also appeared with the following conversions specialized to the lines of operation, premised on local-train operation.

• Changing cross seats near the doors to longitudinal seats
• Further removal of the partitions between vestibule and saloon, and the toilet and washroom equipment
• One-man-operation-compatible cars after the privatization and breakup, etc.
章节.Operations:
The Kiha 58 series began service on each line from 1961, and in the 1980s, with the contraction of limited-express trains, scrapping and transfer to local transport progressed. At the privatization and breakup of JNR in April 1987, this series (excluding the Kiha 56 and 57 series) was inherited by the five passenger JR companies, totaling 1,098 cars.

JR East: 323 cars
JR Central: 103 cars
JR West: 353 cars
JR Shikoku: 131 cars
JR Kyushu: 188 cars

After privatization they continued to be used on limited-express trains and local-line local trains as in the JNR era, and many conversions to Joyful Trains were also carried out. However, from the 1990s scrapping progressed due to replacement from aging, the abolition of limited-express trains, and the end of operations with the electrification of local lines.

One factor in this was the carcinogenicity problem of asbestos, which surfaced in 2005 and became an issue in many quarters. In Japan it had been used in many industrial products, and old railway vehicles also had many examples of its use in interiors and running equipment. Thus, adverse effects on maintenance staff were also discussed in the railway industry. This series was no exception, with asbestos used in car interiors and engine gaskets, and asbestos-scattering prevention work was barely carried out, also from the point of view of aging.

On 11 March 2011, the last scheduled operation of this series — between Toyama and Etchu-Yatsuo on the Takayama Main Line, by cars belonging to the JR West Toyama Regional Railway Department Toyama Driving Center — ended.

With the scrapping of the last stored JR East car on 30 November 2020, the type was eliminated from all JR companies.
章节.East Japan area (JR East):
After privatization they were inherited by JR East, with dedicated liveries applied by allocated depot and line, and were operated mainly on local transport in the Tohoku and Shin'etsu regions. Scrapping progressed through replacement by the Kiha 100 and 110 series, Kiha E130 series and Kiha E120, or knock-on transfers from the introduction of new cars. The last scheduled operation, with three cars belonging to Niitsu Transport District, ended at the 14 March 2009 timetable revision.

From 2011, only the Joyful Train "Kenji" (Kiha 58 650 + Kiha 28 2010 + Kiha 58 1505), belonging to Morioka Rolling Stock Center, was operated on group trains, centered on the temporary rapid "Sanriku Train Miyako" between Morioka and Miyako (via the Yamada Line), mainly on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays outside winter, but it was scrapped in September 2018.

Thereafter, Kiha 58 75 — the last car with registered status across the whole of the JR companies, belonging to Morioka and stored as a reserve car at Akita General Rolling Stock Center — was also scrapped on 30 November 2020, eliminating the type.
章节.Tohoku and the Ou Main Line:
On the Tohoku Main Line, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Miyagi no" between Ueno and Sendai was renamed "Rikuchu" at the 1 October 1961 (Showa 36) San-Roku-To revision, with its extension to Morioka Station, and its cars were replaced with the Kiha 58 series. In December that year it became a three-level train, combined with the Kamaishi Line "Rikuchu" for Miyako and the semi-express "Dai-2 Hayachine" between Morioka and Kamaishi.

In May 1962 they were deployed on the temporary limited express "Dai-2 Bandai" between Ueno and Aizu-Wakamatsu on the Ban'etsu West Line, and the temporary semi-express "Iwashiro" between Koriyama and Aizu-Wakamatsu, which were made scheduled in June that year.

In July 1962 they were deployed on the limited express "Akebono" between Sendai and Aomori (via the Yokoguro Line and Ou Main Line), which became the first premium train on the Yokoguro Line (later the Kitakami Line). The "Akebono" Kiha 58 series was also operated in common with the Sendai–Akita semi-express "Tazawa". On the Uetsu Main Line, from April 1963 they were deployed on the limited express "Shirayuki" between Kanazawa and Aomori (via Niigata Station and the Hakushin Line), coupled with the limited express "Akebono" between Akita and Aomori.

At the October 1963 timetable revision, the limited expresses "Dai-1/Dai-2 Zaou" and "Iide" between Ueno and Yamagata/Niigata (via the Ban'etsu West Line) were newly established, and at the same time the passenger-car limited express "Dewa" between Ueno and Shinjo was diesel-carred and extended to Sakata via the Rikuu West Line. In March 1964 they were deployed on the limited expresses "Dai-2/Dai-1 Zaou/Bandai" between Ueno and Yamagata/Aizu-Wakamatsu, and "Mutsu" between Sendai and Aomori.
章节.Morioka area:
In the final years they belonged to Morioka Rolling Stock Center (Mori-Mori). Scheduled operation on the Yamada Line ended on 24 November 2007 with the introduction of the Kiha 110 series. Kiha 58 1504, 1514 and 1528 were transferred to Myanmar together with the district's Kiha 52. The remaining cars were stored within Morioka Station. All were transferred to and scrapped at Akita General Rolling Stock Center by March 2008.

Thereafter only the Joyful Train "Kenji" continued in operation, but it ended with a group train on 8 September 2018, ending all operation of the series held by JR companies, let alone the district.
章节.Sendai area:
In the final years they belonged to Kogota Transport District (Sen-Koko). Ordinary cars were replaced by the Kiha 110 series by July 2007, ending scheduled operation, but in January 2008 Kiha 58 414 + Kiha 28 2174, former "Gassan" accommodation-conversion cars, were given a revival repainting at Koriyama General Rolling Stock Center, from the Tohoku Regional Headquarters color to the school-excursion color. The formation was used on group and special trains, and a farewell run was held on 23 December 2008, just before the inspection expiry, via the Tohoku Main Line, Ishinomaki Line and Kesennuma Line. On 13 January 2009 they were transferred to Koriyama General Rolling Stock Center for scrapping and dismantled.

The Joyful Train "Kogane" was allocated, but withdrew from service on 26 December 2010 due to aging and was exported overseas.
章节.Kanto area:
In the Kanto area, from June 1962 the Kiha 58 series was deployed on the Joetsu Line and the Naganohara Line (later the Agatsuma Line) semi-express "Kusatsu" and "Kusatsu Iideyu" between Tokyo/Ueno and Naganohara.

In the same month of June 1962, the temporary semi-express "Watarase" between Ueno and Takasaki (via Oyama Station and the Ryomo Line) began operation; "Watarase" was made scheduled at the October revision that year and became a three-level train, combined with the semi-express "Tsukubane" between Ueno and Mito/Moka. The division and coupling of "Watarase" and "Tsukubane" was carried out at Madara Station, and "Tsukubane" did not stop at Oyama Station, entering the Mito Line via the Oyama Shortcut Line.
章节.Chuo East Line: On the Chuo East Line, at the San-Roku-To revision the semi-express "Alps" between Shinjuku and Matsumoto was upgraded to a limited express, and the Kiha 58 series was deployed on "Alps", "Kamikochi" and "Shirouma". In April 1962, through operation of the limited express "Kawaguchi" between Shinjuku and Kawaguchiko by Fuji Kyuko's Kiha 58001 and 002 began, coupled on the Shinjuku–Otsuki section with JNR cars: the limited express "Dai-1 Alps" on the down, and the semi-express "Kaiji" on the up. From June 1963, the Chuo East Line diesel limited-express Kiro 28s were replaced by two-engine Kiro 58s.
章节.Niigata area:
In the Niigata area, the Kiha 58 series was deployed on the limited express "Kitaguni" between Kanazawa and Niigata, which began operation at the 1961 San-Roku-To revision. In 1962 it was deployed on the limited express "Akakura" between Nagoya and Niigata. At the April 1963 revision, with the electrification of Kanazawa on the Hokuriku Main Line, the operating section of "Kitaguni" was extended to between Osaka and Niigata.

In the final years they were allocated to Niitsu Transport District (Ni-Nitsu) and operated on the Ban'etsu West Line, Yonesaka Line and elsewhere, ending scheduled operation at the 14 March 2009 timetable revision. Of these, Kiha 58 1022 + Kiha 28 2371, restored to the former JNR colors in 2003, continued to be used on event trains, and in autumn 2009, as part of a large tourist campaign in the Niigata area, they were also run on the Tadami Line, Iiyama Line and elsewhere, holding farewell operations with Kiha 52 on the Yonesaka Line on 12–13 December and on the Ban'etsu West Line on 26–27 December that year. On 12 January 2010 they were transferred under their own power to Koriyama General Rolling Stock Center and scrapped within that fiscal year.
章节.Tokai area (JR Central): JR Central's inherited cars were used on local transport on the Takayama Main Line, Kisei Main Line, Taketoyo Line and elsewhere, as well as on the limited expresses "Kasuga" and "Norikura" and the rapid "Mie". Until the December 1998 revision there were workings entering JR West territory with Mino-Ota Rolling Stock District cars. Operations ended in 2001, and from 2002 only Kiro 28 2303 remained registered, stored at Mino-Ota Rolling Stock District, but it was scrapped on 31 March 2008 and no cars remained. As a result the Kiro 28 type was eliminated. In February 2013 it was transported by road to Hamamatsu Transport District, and scrapped in October that year.
章节.Chuo West Line: On the Chuo West Line, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Shinano" between Nagoya and Nagano was operated, but at the October 1961 San-Roku-To revision the Honshu Kiha 58 series was deployed for the limited expresses "Shinano", "Shinshu" and "Azumi". The Osaka–Nagano semi-express "Chikuma" was also diesel-carred, with the Shin'etsu Main Line Kiha 57 series deployed on it in common with Shin'etsu-system services.
章节.Takayama Main Line: On the Takayama Main Line, in April 1963 the semi-express "Hida 2" between Nagoya and Kanazawa (via the Takayama Main Line) was upgraded to a limited express, and operated as "Kaetsu" on that section.
章节.West Japan area (JR West):
In the West Japan area, even after the transfer to JR West, cars were deployed on limited-express operations, many of which ran for a while on lines such as the Sanin Main Line, but replacement and scrapping progressed due to the abolition of limited-express trains, the appearance of successor cars such as the Kiha 120 and Kiha 121/126 series, electrification on the Sanin Main Line between Kyoto and Kinosaki Onsen and on the Obama Line, and the aging of and falling demand for Joyful Trains.

The Tsuyama Line limited express "Tsuyama" was replaced from the Kiha 58 series to the Kiha 40 series at the 1 October 2003 revision. At the July 2007 revision, the Geibi Line limited express "Miyoshi" was abolished, and scheduled limited-express trains with the Kiha 58 series disappeared.

The Joyful Train "Honobono SUN-IN" ended operation in November 2009. Ordinary cars — Kiha 58 1114 + Kiha 28 2346 and Kiha 28 2360 + Kiha 58 477, belonging to the Toyama branch (Kin-Toya) of the Toyama Driving Center, Toyama Regional Railway Department — were used on the last scheduled operations of this series in Japan, between Toyama and Etchu-Yatsuo on the Takayama Main Line, from 14 March 2009, but operation ended on 11 March 2011. Thereafter only Kiha 28 2346 remained registered as a reserve car, and its transfer to the Isumi Railway was decided; it was scrapped on 24 July 2012, and on 9 October that year it was removed from Kanazawa General Rolling Stock Works toward Otaki Station (details below).
章节.Hokuriku area:
On the Hokuriku Main Line system, to coincide with the opening of the Hokuriku Tunnel in June 1962 and the electrification between Tsuruga and Fukui, the diesel limited express "Echizen" between Osaka and Kanazawa began operation.

With the 1963 electrification between Fukui and Kanazawa, "Echizen" was electric-carred, and the diesel limited express "Kitaguni" between Osaka and Niigata was established by integrating the passenger-car limited express "Tateyama" between Osaka and Toyama and the Niigata-area limited express "Kitaguni". The Osaka–Wakura/Noto semi-express/limited express "Okunoto", through to the Nanao Line, was also coupled to this train, and when coupled the formation had 12 cars including three Kiro 28s.

After the JR privatization they were also used on local trains on the Oito Line, Takayama Main Line (between Inotani and Toyama), Nanao Line and Obama Line, but scheduled operation ended with the Takayama Main Line in 2011.
章节.Kansai area:
On the Kisei Main Line system, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Kishu" between Nagoya and Tennoji was replaced with the Kiha 58 series from 1 March 1962. The Kiha 58 series was also deployed on the semi-express "Kinokuni" between Shirahama-guchi and Tennoji.

On local trains they were also used on the Katamachi Line and the Kansai Main Line.
章节.Sanyo area:
On the Sanyo Main Line system, at the October 1961 San-Roku-To revision the limited express "Miyajima" between Kyoto and Hiroshima was diesel-carred, and at the same time the limited express "Beppu" between Hiroshima and Beppu was newly established. The Kiha 58 series was also deployed on the Okayama–Hakata limited express "Sanyo", and on the Ogori–Hakata semi-express "Akiyoshi" it was used in a mix with the Kiha 55 series. In 1963, the Hiroshima–Nagasaki limited express "Debushima", coupled with the limited express "Beppu", also began operation.

They were also used on the Sanin–Sanyo connecting limited express "Chidori" and the Geibi Line limited expresses "Miyoshi" and "Taishaku", but with the abolition of "Miyoshi" in 2007, scheduled limited-express trains with the Kiha 58 series disappeared. Of the "Miyoshi" cars, Kiha 58 563 and Kiha 28 2329 were repainted to the former JNR colors at Shimonoseki Rolling Stock Center, Shimonoseki Regional Railway Department (present-day Shimonoseki General Rolling Stock Office), in October 2007, transferring from Hiroshima Driving Office to Okayama Diesel Car District; in November that year they were used on the "Mimasaka Slow Life Train" on the Imbi Line.

Kiha 58 563 and Kiha 28 2329 were also used on special trains in various places, including the Mine Line's "Oidemase Yamaguchi-gō", but withdrew from service after the "Arigatō Kiha 28/58" operated on the Tsuyama Line on 20–21 November 2010, and were later scrapped. Both cars are preserved at the Tsuyama Manabi no Tetsudokan in Tsuyama, Okayama Prefecture.
章节.Sanin area:
On the Sanin Main Line, at the San-Roku-To revision the semi-express "Hakuto" between Kyoto and Yonago was diesel-carred and upgraded to a limited express, with the Kiha 58 series deployed. From October 1962 the Kyoto–Taisha limited express "Daisen" (via the Hakubi Line) was diesel-carred, and from April 1963 this train had its Aioi–Okayama section changed to via the Ako Line, becoming the first premium train on the Ako Line.

In the Sanin area, almost all limited-express trains except those within the area used them: "Sanbe" ran as far as Kumamoto, "Taisha" as far as Nagoya, and there was the 14-car "Inaba", among others. Besides limited expresses, they were used on local trains on the end sections of "Chidori", "Sanbe" and "Misasa", and on the rapid "Tottori Liner", begun in time for the National Sports Festival, but scheduled operation ended at the 1 October 2003 revision with replacement by the Kiha 121/126 series under the Sanin Main Line speed-up project.
章节.Shikoku area (JR Shikoku):
In the Shikoku area, the limited express "Shikoku" between Takamatsu and Uwajima, Shikoku's first limited express, began operation on 15 April 1961, initially with Kiro 28s incorporated into Kiha 55-series formations. At the 1 October 1961 San-Roku-To revision, the limited expresses "Dogo" (Takamatsu–Matsuyama), "Kuroshio" (Takamatsu–Suzaki) and "Urato" (Takamatsu–Kochi) were newly established, and the Kiha 55 series was progressively replaced with the Kiha 58 series.

The district's cars were inherited by JR Shikoku and operated mainly on local trains, but numbers were gradually reduced with the electrification of the Yosan Line between Takamatsu and Iyo-Shi, the introduction of successor 1000- and 1500-series cars, and the upgrading of limited expresses to super expresses with the introduction of the 2000 series and Kiha 185 series. Limited-express operation ended with "Yoshino-gawa", the last, when it was changed to the Kiha 185 series at the March 1998 revision (integrated into the super express "Tsurugisan" in 1999).

Operation on the Takamatsu branch of the Yosan Line ended at the 15 March 2008 timetable revision. The last remaining operation south of Matsuyama on the Yosan Line also ended on 15 October that year, ending all scheduled operation of this series and the Kiha 65. Thereafter, farewell operations were held as "Revival Trains" by Kiha 58 293 + Kiha 65 34 of Matsuyama Driving Office between 18 October and 2 November. At the same time, the "whisker livery" — identifying cars with electronic horns, adopted in the Shikoku district between about 1963 and 1969 — was restored.

On 12 December that year, two JR Shikoku-color cars were used in a comprehensive accident-response drill at Takamatsu Driving Office. All cars including these were scrapped on 31 March 2009.
章节.Kyushu area (JR Kyushu):
In the Kyushu area, from July 1962 the Kagoshima Main Line limited express "Phoenix" between Hakata and Nishi-Kagoshima began operation with the Kiha 58 series. In October that year, the Nippo Main Line limited express "Aoshima" between Moji-ko and Miyazaki was diesel-carred, and "Phoenix" was also operated between Nishi-Kagoshima and Miyazaki. In the same October, the semi-express "Hikari" between Hakata/Moji-ko and Nishi-Kagoshima/Kumamoto was replaced from the Kiha 55 with the Kiha 58 series, and upgraded to a limited express for the first time in four years.

Throughout the JNR era and after the transfer to JR Kyushu, they were used on various lines in Kyushu, mainly non-electrified sections, but scheduled operation by Kagoshima General Rolling Stock Office (present-day Kagoshima Rolling Stock Center) cars ended at the 18 March 2007 timetable revision.

As of 1 April 2018, the following two cars remained registered.

Kiha 58 139 + Kiha 28 2401
Belonging to Kumamoto Rolling Stock Center, Kumamoto Railway Business Department. They were operated as "Aso 1962", the successor to "Aso BOY" — which ended operation with the laying up of the steam locomotive — from 22 July 2006 to 26 December 2010, but even after "Aso 1962" operation ended they were used on group and special trains. They were later preserved as reserve cars at Kumamoto Rolling Stock Center, but were transferred to Kokura General Rolling Stock Center in late March 2018. Kiha 28 2401 was scrapped on 16 January 2019, and Kiha 58 139 on 23 January that month.

Also, these two cars were the last registered cars of this series with original bodies and DMH17H engines across the entire JR Group.
章节.Sister cars: As examples of private railways ordering limited-express diesel railcars of the same type as JNR cars for the purpose of through operation into JNR lines, there is the case of Fuji Kyuko with the Kiha 58 series. Similar cases are seen with Nankai Electric Railway's Kiha 5501 and 5551, which ordered sister cars of the Kiha 55 series, and the Shimabara Railway's Kiha 55 and Kiha 26.
章节.Fuji Kyuko Kiha 58:
From 1962 (Showa 37), the limited express "Kawaguchi", coupled with the Chuo Main Line limited express "Alps" from Otsuki Station on the Fuji Kyuko Line, ran through to Shinjuku Station. Although the Fuji Kyuko Line and the Chuo Main Line between Shinjuku and Otsuki were entirely DC-electrified sections, the coupled limited express "Alps" was necessarily a diesel train, as it ran through to non-electrified sections, so Fuji Kyuko needed its own dedicated cars for coupling, and Kiha 58001 and 58002 were built by Nippon Sharyo in December 1961 (Showa 36). In 1963 (Showa 38), Kiha 58003 was built as a spare car.

As the Chuo Main Line and Fuji Kyuko Line are steeply graded lines, with sections of 40 per mille, they were made Kiha 58 type with two engines, and although the exterior color and passenger accommodation were the same, they differed from JNR-specification cars in the following points.

• The car numbers were five digits, as on JNR former-type electric cars and former-type diesel railcars.
• As they normally formed two-car sets with Kiha 58001 and 58002, both cars were single-cab cars with toilet and washroom, the same as the JNR specification.
• Kiha 58003, from the viewpoint of a spare car, needed to be able to form on either side of a set, so it was built as the only double-cab car newly built in the Kiha 58 series. To match the capacity of single-cab cars while maintaining overall length and seat pitch, all passenger doors were narrowed in width and the vestibule shortened, and the space from abolishing the toilet and washroom was changed to four-person box seats, with the vestibule windows in that section made wide and large with fixed H rubber. Other external differences: there is no water tank on the roof; the front-side vestibule window is slightly narrower; and all passenger doors are compatible with the fitting of tablet protective frames.

From 1969 onward, JNR cars were progressively air conditioned, but Fuji Kyuko's cars were not air-conditioning converted, and with the electric-carring of all "Alps" trains in March 1975 they lost their purpose, and were scrapped on 24 April that year in exchange for the appearance of the Fuji Kyuko 5000 series. Thereafter, 58001 and 58002 had their toilets and washrooms removed, and all three cars were transferred in July that year to the Arita Railway, where through trains into JNR lines were also operated, beginning service in May 1976. They replaced that company's Kiha 07.

The Arita Railway Line is flat along its entire length, and from the viewpoint of reducing running costs, all cars were converted to single-engine at JNR Takasago Works in 1980. Also, as passenger numbers continued to decline, the double-cab 58003, capable of single-car operation, was often used, and with the start of operation of the air-conditioned Haimo 180-101 transferred from Tarumi Railway in June 1994, 58001 and 58002, whose utilization rate had long been falling, were scrapped in November that year. 58003 remained as a spare car until that railway's abolition in 2002.
章节.Transferred cars:
As this series was used by JNR and then JR, the following seven cars in total were transferred to railway operators in Japan.

Kita-Kinki Tango Railway: 4 cars (see below)
Arita Railway: Kiha 58 136, Kiha 58 86
Isumi Railway: Kiha 28 2346 (see below)

There are also examples of transfer to the Sakhalin Railway of Russian Railways, the State Railway of Thailand and Myanmar Railways abroad.
章节.Kita-Kinki Tango Railway KTR1000 and KTR:
In fiscal 1989, four cars of this series were transferred, for use on supplementary limited expresses to the KTR001 "Tango Explorer".

Types
KTR1000 (1001, 1002)
KTR2000 (2001, 2002)

KTR1000s were former Kiha 28s and KTR2000s former Kiha 58s; the type names derive from the number of engines carried.

Kiha 58 591 + Kiha 28 2198 → KTR2001 + KTR1001 (former owner: JNR Settlement Corporation)
Kiha 58 102 + Kiha 28 2314 → KTR2002 + KTR1002 (former owner: JR West)

Conversions carried out at the transfer: JR West Tottori Works carried out the work.

• The exterior livery was changed to silver metallic-based, with the corporate color Chitose-green plus Tobi-red lines below the windows.
• KTR1000s had their toilet and washroom removed and changed to a baggage space.
• Formation 2 (1002, 2002) had a front-end shape following JR West's Kiha 65 "Edel", and observation seats arranged stair-like.
• Formation 2's observation-room seats were exchanged for free-stop reclining seats with large back tables, with green seat moquette. The general-room seats of formations 1 and 2 were exchanged for rotating reclining seats modified from limited-express electric cars' simple reclining seats, with green moquette, as in the observation seats.

This type was named "Rainbow Resort", and also operated through into JR lines as three- or four-car formations, with formation 2 alone or formation 1 (1001, 2001) inserted in the middle, but KTR1002 and KTR2002 were scrapped and dismantled on 7 June 1995, and KTR1001 and KTR2001 on 24 January 1996, replaced by the new KTR8000 "Tango Discovery".
章节.Isumi Railway Kiha 28 2346:
On 27 August 2012, the company's then-president Ryo Torizuka announced the transfer from JR West on his blog, and the car was delivered on 11 October that year.

Unlike Kiha 52 125, it was maintained at Kanazawa General Rolling Stock Works and repainted from the Takaoka color to the JNR limited-express color before transfer, then maintained again on the Isumi Railway. Revenue operation began on 9 March 2013. In revenue operation it forms a train with Kiha 52 125 and is coupled on the Ohara Station side.

The car was built as Kiha 28 346 by Teikoku Sharyo in 1964 and newly allocated to Yonago Engine Depot (present-day Goto General Rolling Stock Office) on 15 April that year. On 24 May that year it transferred to Niigata Engine Depot (present-day Niigata Rolling Stock Center), on 14 July to Chiba Diesel Car Depot, where it was used for beachgoer transport in the Boso area, and on 17 September back to Yonago Engine Depot — in effect loan-like transfers. In 1972 it was air-conditioned and fitted with a 4VK generator set, and renumbered 2346. It continued to be used in the Sanin area. In 1985 it transferred to Nanao Engine Depot (present-day Nanao Railway Department), and was inherited by JR West at privatization. In 1991 it transferred to Toyama Driving Office, and in 1996 to Takaoka Railway Department. In 2000 it transferred once to Obama, but with the electrification of the Obama Line in 2003 it transferred to Takaoka again. It later became a reserve car, but in 2004 it was loaned to Echizen-Ono Railway Department and used for disaster restoration on the Etsumi-Hoku Line. After this it always formed trains with Kiha 58 1114, and in 2007 transferred to Toyama with a trial increase in trains on the Takayama Main Line. It was operated on the Takayama Main Line in the Takaoka color.

As of 2022, it was the only operating car of this series in revenue service in Japan, but scheduled operation ended on 27 November 2022; the full inspection — costing about 100 million yen for parts re-manufacture and other work — was abandoned, support was sought by crowdfunding, and as of February 2024 it is statically preserved at Kuniyoshi Station, but from February 2024 crowdfunding was again carried out for panel beating and repainting, as rust from body corrosion and paint deterioration had become severe. Furthermore, in future the Isumi Railway plans experiential riding and driving experiences using these two cars and the Kiha 58, JNR-type diesel railcars, and has announced that, while aiming at the "Rail Park" concept — the development of a tourist facility where people can enjoy railway vehicles — it will target new promotion of railway use and the development of tourist demand using these vehicles, which are also Showa-era industrial heritage.
章节.Exports abroad: Given this series' versatility and large numbers, there were cars donated free of charge abroad after scrapping. From JR East they were donated to Russia's Sakhalin Oblast, and from JR West to Thailand and Myanmar. There are also cars exported from JR West to the People's Republic of China, but they have been left abandoned at their destination.
章节.Russian Federation Ministry of Transport:
At the Far Eastern Railway Sakhalin Branch of the Soviet Ministry of Transport, ten D2-series trains (40 cars) built by Fuji Heavy Industries were introduced in 1985 via Nissho Iwai to replace Japanese-made A1-series diesel railcars (introduced 1963), and used for commuter passenger transport; after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the Sakhalin Railway of the Russian Federation Ministry of Transport inherited them, but with high inflation and budget shortages from the economic chaos after democratization, parts could not be procured, and maintenance of the D2 series became difficult.

In August 1992, a delegation of railway engineers from JR East and others visited the Sakhalin Railway, and in January 1993 a Sakhalin Railway delegation visited Japan and toured JR East and JR West stations, travel centers and works; this was the impetus for the signing of a free vehicle-transfer contract between the Sakhalin Railway and JR East in October that year, and 29 Kiha 58s were exported from Ichihara Port, Chiba Prefecture, to Kholmsk Port.

After arrival locally, they were transferred under their own power from Kholmsk–Sol'tsilovochny Station to the Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk Engine Depot, and 17 cars, excluding parts-donor cars, were maintained. As the K-1 type (K-01 onward), they began operation on commuter passenger trains from April 1994. With the recovery of the Russian economy, the budget shortage was resolved, and all cars ended operation in 2000 when the D2 series returned to service. One car is statically preserved.
章节.Thailand:
In 1997, a total of 26 cars — 14 Kiha 58, 9 Kiha 28 and 3 Kiro 28 — and in 1999 a total of 20 cars — 11 Kiha 58 and 9 Kiha 28 — 46 cars in all, were donated free of charge.

The State Railway of Thailand carried out modifications including re-gauging to 1 m, changes to the brake system, and the fitting of steps at the doors. Local type names: former Kiha 58s became the 100 series, former Kiha 28s the 200 series, and former Kiro 28s the 300 series.

Initially they were used on premium trains, but around 2000 the engines were removed and the air conditioning stopped being used, and they came to be used on local trains as substitutes for third-class passenger cars. Today the cabs and engines have been completely removed and the air conditioning is unused. The following causes are estimated.

• The cabs are on the opposite side from the local standard, making them awkward for recognizing signals and handing over staff and tokens.
• They were already aged and heavily deteriorated.
• The formations were haphazard, preventing appropriate operation; the discontinuation of air conditioning also stemmed from this.
• The bodies were large, exceeding the State Railway of Thailand's loading gauge, causing problems in tunnels and on sharp curves.

Later, large-scale refreshment work — cab removal and door relocation — was carried out on some cars. Until around 2005 they were repainted to gray with blue and white gradients (end faces plain yellow) and used on passenger trains in the Bangkok metropolitan area, but today most cars are laid up or scrapped. However, some cars are used as service vehicles, and with the aim of replacing aging old passenger cars, improvement work shortening the car bodies to cope with sharp curves has been carried out on some cars, though it has not led to service.

Separately from the above cars, the transfer of the "Resort Saloon Festa" was also planned, but was canceled for reasons on the Thai side. The severe aging of the donor cars was also a factor.

Reference site: State Railway of Thailand Friends Association — Wayback Machine (5 April 2003 archive)
章节.Myanmar: In 2008, three Kiha 58s were donated free of charge by JR East. After transfer, large-scale conversion work was carried out, including re-gauging to 1 m gauge, lowering the roof height in view of Myanmar Railways' loading gauge, and removal of the air-conditioning units. Initially they were used on limited-express trains, and today they are used on Yangon suburban trains. Even before this, cars had been donated by JR West.
章节.China: Kiha 28 2306 and Kiha 28 2486, exported after scrapping in 2004, have been confirmed to have been left abandoned for a long time in the bonded zone of Tianjin Port at two points in 2013 and 2018.
章节.Accident write-offs:
Nine cars were written off in accidents, including during the JNR era and after JR privatization. For details of the accidents, see the linked pages.

Kiha 58 666
The car involved in the limited express "Yoshino-gawa" derailment accident that occurred on 14 October 1969. Formed at the head, the car collided with a dump truck and derailed heavily. Scrapped on 12 March 1970.

Kiha 58 1034
On 15 May 1973, while operating on the Nagoya–Tennoji limited express "Kishu 1", it collided with a dump truck at a level crossing between Sana and Tochihara on the Kisei Main Line. The car, formed at the head, suffered major front damage. Scrapped on 8 March 1974.

Kiha 58 409, 1015; Kiha 28 2005, 2352
The train involved in the Noto Line train derailment accident that occurred on 11 July 1985; the four-car limited express "Notoji 5". All cars were scrapped on 1 October that year.

Kiro 59 508
The car involved in the Salon Express Arcadia fire accident that occurred on 30 March 1988; it was completely burned out from a fire caused by exhaust-pipe overheating and scrapped.

Kiha 58 1023
The car involved in the Shigaraki Kogen Railway train collision accident that occurred on 14 May 1991. The car was formed at the head of the special train "Sekai Tōgeishi Shigarakigō", a three-car train of this series through-operated from JR West to the Shigaraki Kogen Railway. Between Onoya Signal Field and Shigarakigūshi-ato Station on the Shigaraki Line, it collided head-on with a four-car Shigaraki Kogen Railway SKR200-series diesel railcar formation and derailed heavily. As the body was bent, restoration was difficult, and it was scrapped on 31 March 1994.

Kiha 28 3013
On 26 August 2003, while operating on Dosan Line local train 226D from Kochi Station to Awa-Ikeda Station, the driver noticed that the 4VK engine for air-conditioning power was rotating faster than usual; near Gomen the driver tried to stop the 4VK engine but could not, and it was stopped by a maintenanceman waiting at Tosa-Yamada Station, but white smoke flowed into the car. A fire broke out from the floor at Awa-Kawaguchi Station, and passengers were evacuated and firefighting carried out.

The cause was that a part of the 4VK engine came off, causing over-supply of fuel and abnormal combustion, which abnormally overheated the muffler; however, as replacement of this type was progressing, repairs were not carried out, and after being laid up it was scrapped on 31 March 2004.
章节.Preserved cars: In this section, operationally preserved, statically preserved, preserved-then-scrapped, and abroad-preserved cars are explained. For preserved cars of the Kiha 56 series, see here.
章节.Cars preserved abroad:
Russian Federation Ministry of Transport K-1 K-01 (Kiha 58 495)
Preserved from 2006 onward at the Russian Railways Sakhalin Railway History Museum in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, Sakhalin Oblast.

State Railway of Thailand 101 (Kiha 58) and 209 (Kiha 28)
Scrapped car bodies repainted and internally refitted, used as a train library in front of Hua Hin Station.

英文.全文:
The Kiha 58 series (キハ58系気動車) is a class of limited-express diesel railcars (diesel multiple units) built by Japanese National Railways (JNR) from 1961.

They were built in large numbers until 1969, and from the 1960s to the 1980s were used on limited-express services throughout Japan, on trunk and local lines alike.

The expression "Kiha 58 series" used in this article is a convenient general term for the diesel railcars built to a common design concept; it is not an official designation. In the broad sense it includes the "Kiha 56 series" for Hokkaido and the "Kiha 57 series" built to cope with the rack-rail section over the Usui Pass (between Yokokawa and Karuizawa stations), but this article mainly describes the narrow-sense "Kiha 58". Specifically, it covers the five types — Kiro 28, Kiro 58, Kiha 28, Kiha 58 and KiYu 25 — and conversions of these.

This article also describes Fuji Kyuko's own-order cars and cars transferred to other operators.

== Overview ==
In the 1960s they were mass-produced with the aim of replacing steam-locomotive-hauled trains, achieving higher speeds and improved comfort and habitability, and eliminating smoke. They were a family of vehicles that completed a nationwide network of diesel-railcar limited-express trains on both trunk and local lines.

They were operated in 45 prefectures, excluding Shizuoka Prefecture and Okinawa Prefecture, which had no JNR or JR presence.

From the 1970s onward, the electrification of trunk lines progressed rapidly, and limited-express trains were progressively converted to electric multiple units or upgraded to super-express trains, so diesel-railcar limited expresses gradually narrowed their sphere of operation, and from the 1980s many were transferred to local-train duties on local lines.

At the time of the privatization and breakup of JNR in 1987 (Showa 62), about two-thirds of the total fleet was taken over by the JR companies. Many of them were operated on non-electrified local lines as local trains after suburban-type conversions and one-man-operation conversions, while others had their seats upgraded in grade and were used on rapid services on regional trunk lines; some cars, meanwhile, were converted for the dedicated group trains known as "Joyful Trains". However, due to aging, the building of successor types, the electrification of routes serving regional core cities and the resulting replacement by electric trains, or the abolition of deficit-making local lines, withdrawals and scrapping progressed, and with the scrapping of the last stored car on 30 November 2020 (Reiwa 2), they disappeared completely from JR trunk lines.

== Background to development ==
From the late 1950s, the modernization of motive power saw diesel-railcar semi-express trains begin operation in various parts of Japan, producing major gains in speed, comfort and habitability, and a movement arose to switch limited-express trains on non-electrified main trunk lines from passenger-car trains hauled by steam locomotives to diesel railcars.

The Type 55 series, then used for semi-express trains, met the performance standards required at the time and some were quickly pressed into limited-express service, but third-class cars had no separate washroom, and second-class cars had non-reclining rotating cross seats, so as limited-express vehicles they were inferior in passenger-service facilities to the conventional passenger cars. It was therefore decided to develop a diesel railcar with running performance equal to that of the Type 55 series but with facilities fully adequate for limited-express service, and this series was the result.

In the development process, experience was fed back from the Type 60 series, high-output diesel railcars prototyped in 1959 (Showa 34), and from the Type 80 series, Japan's first limited-express diesel railcars, which appeared in 1960 (Showa 35).

== Construction ==

=== Car body ===
The body livery used beige (cream No. 4) as the base color, with the window surrounds, lower skirt and rain gutters painted scarlet (red No. 11). The color of the gutters was progressively changed to beige.

As a diesel railcar, they adopted a wide body and a floating-floor structure, following the limited-express Kiha 80 series. The body width was increased by 100 mm over the Kiha 55 series to 2,944 mm, so the lower part of the body was tucked in to avoid infringing the vehicle loading gauge; and to prevent the rain gutters from bulging beyond the loading gauge when the body rolled on curves and striking lineside equipment, a comparatively rarely used raised-roof structure was adopted for a JNR vehicle. This placed the rain gutters at the shoulder of the roof and widened the valance panel.

In addition to the gangway already standardized on diesel railcars, the front end adopted the design philosophy of the Kuha 153-500 series built at the same period: a high-cab structure in case of level-crossing accidents, with a train-type indicator blind above the gangway. However, the headlights were made two small shield-beam lamps split to the left and right at the top of the cab, and for cost reduction the curved "panoramic window" glass wrapping around into the body corners — which remained standard on limited-express and suburban electric cars for years afterward — was omitted in favor of flat glass extending to the full width of the body; the lower-body skirt was also omitted.

Passenger doors were widened to 850 mm, wider than on the Kiha 55 series. Furthermore, whereas the Kiha 55 series had a simplified arrangement with the toilet at the car end and — except on the Kiroha 25 and Kiro 25 — no separate washroom, this series placed the toilet and washroom between the car-end vestibule (deck) and the saloon. However, only on the Kiro 28 300 and 500 series (the +2000 cars fitted with the 4VK generator set) was a design change made to place them outside the end vestibule.

On the two-engine Kiha 58 and Kiro 58, water tanks for the toilet and washroom were carried on the roof, as the underfloor equipment left little mounting space.

=== Passenger compartment equipment ===
By adopting horizontal-cylinder engines, engine maintenance became possible from the side beneath the floor, and the inspection hatches in the saloon floor fitted to conventional diesel railcars were abolished. This improved quietness and habitability. The floor finish was vinyl on cars for south of Honshu, while only the Kiha 56 series for Hokkaido had wooden flooring, improving thermal insulation and durability against the metal studs on snow boots. In addition, the exhaust pipe, previously routed up the central wall of the saloon, was moved to both ends of the car body outside the passenger area (on single-engine cars, only the front end), improving sight lines and appearance inside the car. These improvements followed those of the limited-express Kiha 80 series developed earlier.

Second-class cars (present-day ordinary cars) are fitted with twenty bays (80 seats' worth) of facing four-person cross seats (box seats) with large one-step rising windows, but there is one row of two-person seats by the vestibule window on the cab side, making a total capacity of 84. The wider body allowed elbow-width space by the windows, as on limited-express electric cars, and small tables with bottle openers and large ashtrays were installed below the window frames. Whereas conventional diesel railcars generally used incandescent lamps for lighting, this series adopted 40 W straight-tube fluorescent lamps to brighten the interior.

First-class cars (present-day Green cars) adopted reclining seats — standard on first-class passenger cars for limited-express trains — together with one-step dropping twin side windows like those of the Saha 152, but the milky-white fluorescent-lamp covers adopted on the Saha 152 were omitted for cost reduction.

The one-step dropping windows: by the late 1970s, body corrosion from the ingress and stagnation of rainwater had become serious, and although drainage countermeasures were taken — including on all cars that adopted them, such as the 157-series electric cars — these were inadequate, and many surviving adopters, including the Saha 165 and Saha 455, had their side windows exchanged for outer-hung unit windows of upper-drop, lower-rise type in the 1980s.

The class band on the earliest-delivered Kiro 26, 27 and 28 was blue No. 1, but as the class band was changed to pale green No. 6 in July 1961 (Showa 36), second-batch cars onward were delivered in the new band color. Blue-band cars were also repainted to pale green No. 6 within a short time.

For heating: conventional diesel railcars had light-oil-fired forced-air heaters as standard, but in some cases the heat output was insufficient. As the hot-water heating system using engine cooling water, adopted on the Kiha 22 — a cold-resistant enhanced type developed for Hokkaido in 1958 (Showa 33) — had shown good results, it was adopted on this series too, improving heating efficiency and quietness.

A radiator carrying the high-temperature cooling water after engine cooling is installed at the passengers' feet to provide heating, but its drawback is that it encroaches on the foot space by the windows.

In addition, on the Kiha 56 series for Hokkaido, water pipes sharing the supply source of the interior heating were also fitted in places such as the horn shutters and behind the passenger-door steps (door rails), from the viewpoint of preventing freezing in winter.

=== Main machinery ===
They were equipped with the horizontal-cylinder DMH17H diesel engine (180 PS / 1,500 rpm) developed in 1960 as a limited-express diesel engine, combined with a Shinko Zoki TC-2A or Niigata Converter DF115A, the conventional standard liquid transmission.

Engine output and transmission were unchanged from the late-model Kiha 55 series, and running performance was equivalent. Although the conventional vertical cylinders were redesigned as horizontal cylinders, the basic structure is the same un-supercharged pre-combustion-chamber type, which was already obsolete by 1961.

Bogies were the standard metal-spring DT22A and DT22C (powered) and TR51A and TR51B (trailer), as on the late-model Kiha 55 series.

These are clearly a grade below the air-sprung bogies that were already standard on contemporary JNR limited-express electric cars, but their adoption prioritized cost reduction because of the need to mass-produce vehicles for regional lines — and moreover cab-equipped vehicles.

However, the Kiha 57 and Kiro 27 were fitted with DT31 and TR68 bogies using disc brakes and bellows-type air springs as bolster springs, capable of maintaining a constant car height, as it was necessary to avoid interference between the rack rail laid in the center of the track on the Yokokawa–Karuizawa section of the Shin'etsu Main Line — then of the Abt rack type — and the bogies' foundation brake gear and underfloor equipment.

The brake system is fundamentally the DA1 automatic air brake, controlling body-mounted brake cylinders with the A operating valve, then standard for diesel railcars, but the Kiha 57 series, for compatibility with the aforementioned disc brakes, adopted DAR1 on cab-equipped Kiha cars — adding a relay valve to the DA1-series brake system to make it a bogie-cylinder type — and the cabless Kiro adopted the DAR2 automatic air brake.

== Types ==
The "broad Kiha 58 series" comprises three series: the cold- and snow-resistant "Kiha 56 series" for Hokkaido, the "Kiha 57 series" equipped with air-sprung bogies for the Shin'etsu Main Line, and the narrow-sense "Kiha 58 series", the standard type for south of Honshu. The total of 1,823 cars built across the broad Kiha 58 series is the largest number of diesel railcars in Japanese history, and at one time they accounted for 30 percent of all diesel railcars on JNR's books. The manufacturers were five companies: Niigata Engineering, Fuji Heavy Industries, Nippon Sharyo, Teikoku Sharyo and Tokyu Car.

In addition to the above, the KiYu 25 existed as a newly built type owned by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (as it then was). For types and sub-series created by conversion, see the section on conversions and refurbishment.

Unlike limited-express electric cars, no half-buffet cars were built.

=== For Hokkaido (Kiha 56 series) ===
The Kiha 55 series used on Honshu was not designed for Hokkaido, and due to vehicle shortages, semi-express and limited-express trains within Hokkaido also used general-purpose Kiha 22s. To resolve the vehicle shortage in the Hokkaido district, the first limited-express diesel railcars were introduced for Hokkaido in March 1961, with the Kiha 56, Kiha 27 and Kiro 26 appearing.

The basic design was the same as the later Kiha 58 series for Honshu, but severe-cold design features were adopted, such as small double side windows and wooden flooring. The bogies were coil-spring DT22 and TR51 series.

Operations began in March 1961 on the Nemuro Main Line limited express "Karigachi".

=== For the Shin'etsu Main Line (Kiha 57 series) ===
In 1961, the Yokokawa–Karuizawa section of the Shin'etsu Main Line (the Yokokaru section) crossing the Usui Pass was of the Abt rack type, and diesel railcars using conventional DT22-series bogies could not pass it, as their brake gear interfered with the rack rail. To coincide with the Zenkoji temple gokaicho (special public opening) held in Nagano that year, and ahead of the cars for south of Honshu, the Kiha 57 and Kiro 27 — modified to pass the rack section — appeared in April 1961 for the Shin'etsu Main Line. The bogies were DT31 and TR68 series using air springs and disc brakes.

Operations began in April 1961 on the Shin'etsu Main Line limited express "Shiga". The Yokokaru section was replaced by a new adhesion-type line in 1963, ending the rack system, so use of the Kiha 57 series for its original purpose lasted only about two years. Thereafter they were used in various parts of Honshu and Shikoku, mixed with the Honshu Kiha 58 series.

=== For south of Honshu (Kiha 58 series) ===
To expand the limited-express network in the Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu districts, the Kiha 58 series — the mainstay for south of Honshu — was introduced from May 1961, with the Kiha 58, Kiha 28 and Kiro 28 appearing. The bogies were coil-spring DT22 and TR51 series, as on the Kiha 56 series. The Kiro 58 was added in 1962.

The basic type was built up from 1961 (Showa 36), and was also pressed into the limited expresses newly established across the country at the 1 October San-Roku-To timetable revision. The 800 series for school excursions also appeared in 1962. An improved type for long formations appeared in 1963, and in the case of the Kiha 58 this was numbered the 400 series. From 1968, model-change cars appeared with curved front windows and skirts, this group being divided into warm-region and cold-region versions.

When air-conditioning conversions were later carried out, a system was adopted in which single-engine cars such as the Kiha 28 carried power-supply equipment and fed the other cars. Mainly fitted were the 4DQ on the Kiro 28 — supplying its own car only — and the 4VK on the Kiha 28, capable of supplying up to three cars including its own. On mountain routes requiring high output, the Kiha 65, equipped with high-output engines and air-conditioning power supplies, was also introduced.

=== KiYu 25 ===
Private postal cars owned by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications. They were the only all-postal-compartment cars among diesel railcars, and all were built by Niigata Engineering. Structurally, Nos. 1 and 2, built in 1964, correspond to long-formation-compatible cars, and Nos. 3 and 4, built in 1971, to model-change cars.

The interior, following on from the cab, had a parcel-closing mail-bag room, a rest room and mail-sorting room in the center, and ordinary-closing mail-bag rooms and a toilet at the rear. Since the 1960s, newly built all-postal-compartment cars had been equipped with air conditioning to improve the postal staff's working environment, and this type was fitted from new with four AU13 (Nos. 1 and 2) or AU13A (Nos. 3 and 4) distributed air-conditioning units, plus a 4DQ generator set for self-supply. A distinguishing feature is that even Nos. 1 and 2, belonging to the long-formation-compatible group, had a roof height as low as that of Nos. 3 and 4 of the final batch group. Also, as there was no supply, receipt or pass-through of air-conditioning power to other cars, the KE53 air-conditioning-control and KE8 power-supply jumper couplers were not fitted.

All cars were allocated to Takamatsu Driving Office and operated in the Shikoku district, but ahead of the abolition of railway postal services, all were scrapped on 6 June 1986 (Showa 61).

The improvements were wide-ranging, and where a major improvement was carried out, a numbered sub-series distinction was applied.

=== 800 series (for school excursions) ===
A numbered sub-series for school-excursion trains in the Tohoku and Kyushu districts. A total of 32 cars — 19 Kiha 58 and 13 Kiha 28 — were built between 1962 and 1963 by Tokyu Car and Teikoku Sharyo (the latter for the Kiha 58 only).

The body structure basically followed the general-specification cars, but the interior was equipped following the style of the 155- and 159-series electric cars of the same period, which were for school excursions. As with the standard cars of this series, the seating was four-per-bay box seats and the luggage racks ran in the rail direction, but additional equipment was fitted: auxiliary deck seats, an in-car speedometer, removable folding large tables, a large washstand usable by three people side by side, and pull-out simple beds for sick passengers at the saloon ends. The livery, although its color division followed the standard type, reversed that of the 155 and 159 series — window surrounds and skirt in yellow No. 5 with vermilion No. 3 — giving a design common to school-excursion use.

Dedicated school-excursion trains with this numbered sub-series ran as "Omoide" between the Tohoku district and Tokyo, and "Tobiume" between the Kyushu district and the Kansai area. Outside the school-excursion season they were also used on special trains and, with formations broken up, in single-car units on scheduled trains. By the late 1970s, however, these trains ended with the extension of the Sanyo Shinkansen to Hakata Station and the development of the limited-express network on the Tohoku Main Line. Thereafter the livery was progressively changed to the limited-express color from 1978 (Showa 53), but air-conditioning conversions and removal of the school-excursion equipment were left undone, and they were mixed with standard cars of this series and Type 55 cars, mainly on local trains; in the Tohoku district, where the air conditioning of diesel limited expresses lagged, they were also used on limited-express trains. All cars were scrapped between 1984 (Showa 59) and 1987 (Showa 62), so none were inherited by the JR passenger companies.

=== Long-formation-compatible cars ===
JNR diesel railcars had in common multiple-unit control via two KE53 jumper couplers on a DC 24 V supply, and automatic brakes actuated by air pressure. As the control circuits operated each car's control devices on the leading car's power, there were problems of capacity and voltage drop in the power supply and through-wires; and as the brakes were air-pressure controlled, there was a problem of delayed response by cars at the rear of the formation. Long formations with this series were initially restricted to a maximum of 11 cars with 17 engines.

Therefore, from the fifth batch of limited-express diesel railcars, built from fiscal 1963 (Showa 38) onward, the following changes were made.

• Electromagnetic application and release solenoid valves were added close to the auxiliary air reservoir beneath each car's floor, and in the footwell of the cab on cab-equipped cars, to improve brake response.
• The cab's M23-series brake control valve was changed to the ME23B valve, capable of commanding the electromagnetic solenoid valves; cab-equipped cars were changed to the DAE1, and cabless Kiro cars to the DAE2, electromagnetic automatic air brake.
• Through-wiring via KE67 jumper couplers was added for the control circuits in connection with the DAE brake conversion.
• The control circuits were arranged so that each car had an auxiliary relay and each car's control circuit operated on that car's own power, improving through-wire voltage drop and the capacity limits on control current.

As a result, up to 15 cars with 23 engines could be controlled. Groups built from the outset for long-formation operation were given new number-series distinctions.

=== Model-change cars ===
The group built from 1968 (Showa 43) to 1969 (Showa 44). Running performance was unchanged, but minor body changes and other improvements were made, as follows.

Ordinary cars received air-conditioning-preparation work so that seven AU13 distributed air-conditioning units could be simply bolted on, in anticipation of later air conditioning. For this reason the roof shape became flatter than before, and lower, the same as the Kiro 28 139 onward that became newly built air-conditioned cars within the long-formation group. == Air-conditioning conversions ==
Until the first half of the 1960s, air conditioning on JNR trains was limited to premium cars such as limited-express trains and some dining cars (including buffet cars), but on limited-express trains, first-class cars were progressively air conditioned from 1963 (Showa 38) and second-class cars from 1968 (Showa 43).

The Kiro 26, 27, 28 and 58 completed the air conditioning of their non-air-conditioned and air-prep cars by fiscal 1968. Of the ordinary cars, all 36 Kiha 57s were air conditioned, but air conditioning of the Kiha 58 and 28, for which surpluses were certain given the upgrading of limited expresses, was suspended in 1980 (Showa 55), leaving about 670 cars non-air-conditioned, and many cars were scrapped in that state, mainly in the Tohoku region. For the Hokkaido Kiha 56 and 27, although the improved 200 series were delivered as air-prep cars, no air-conditioning conversion at all was carried out, including on the earlier non-air-conditioned cars; after inheritance by Hokkaido Railway Company (JR Hokkaido), only a group converted into Joyful Trains and a very small number of cars were air conditioned.

=== Air conditioning of first-class and Green cars (Kiro) ===

==== Prototype air-conditioning conversion using bus air conditioning ====
On this series, a conversion was carried out and tested in 1963–64 on five cars — Kiro 28 26, 53, 54, 62 and 65 — allocated to the Kyushu district: BAU102 air-conditioning units were fitted beneath the floor at Kokura Works (present-day Kokura General Rolling Stock Center), driven directly by a 45 PS in-line four-cylinder bus/truck diesel engine, and a trial was conducted.

This method had the advantage of low conversion cost, but it was not adopted due to various problems, including frequent failures later, and the test cars were all converted in 1968 (Showa 43) to AU13 units with 4DQ power equipment.

==== Prototype air-conditioning conversion with the AU12 ====
Full air-conditioning conversion of the Kiro 28 and 58 adopted the system of mounting distributed air-conditioning units on the roof, powered by three-phase alternating current, as on limited-express and limited-express-type electric cars. This required a large-capacity AC supply, but the alternator (generator) attached to a diesel railcar's traction engine was designed only to the extent of securing the power for engine starting, control, safety, lighting and in-car announcements, and engine performance left no margin to drive a large-capacity, high-load generator. Non-air-conditioned and air-prep Kiro 26, 27 and 28 cars were successively converted, while newly built cars carried independent engine-driven air-conditioning units from the outset, securing air-conditioning power for their own car alone.

In 1963, two cars, Kiro 28 109 and 110, were converted to carry the AU12 (4,000 kcal/h) used for limited-express-type cars. Six AU12 units were mounted on the roof, with a 4DQ-11P engine for small trucks/microbuses and a DM72 generator below the floor as the air-conditioning power supply. A distribution board was provided in the attendant's room, ventilation was by forced-draft fans, and the roof ventilators were abolished.

==== Full air conditioning of non-air-conditioned Kiro 28 cars ====
The AU12 was judged to have insufficient capacity for limited-express diesel railcars, and subsequent air conditioning used the AU13 (5,500 kcal/h) developed for limited-express cars. From fiscal 1965 to fiscal 1968 it was applied as "Kiro car air-conditioning work A" to all Kiro 27s and the non-air-conditioned Kiro 26 and 28; six AU13 units were mounted on the roof, with a 4DQ engine and DM72A generator (the DM72 made smaller and lighter) below the floor, and a distribution board in the attendant's room. Ventilation was not of the forced-draft type, and the roof ventilators were retained.

==== Air conditioning of air-conditioning-prepared Kiro 28 cars ====
This work targeted the 36 cars newly built as air-prep cars — Kiro 26 104–107 and Kiro 28 111–133, 145, 146, 153, 154 — and was carried out as "Kiro car air-conditioning work B" from fiscal 1966 to fiscal 1968. Six AU13 units were mounted on the roof, with a 4DQ engine and DM72A generator below the floor and a distribution board in the attendant's room, but as they were force-ventilated from new, there were no ventilators other than in the attendant's room.

==== Air conditioning of the Kiro 58 ====
The Kiro 58, operated on the Chuo Main Line, had no underfloor space as a two-engine car, so in fiscal 1968 it received "Kiro car air-conditioning work C", a conversion fitting only the air-conditioning units, with power supplied from the 4VK generator sets of Kiha 28 1505–1510.

==== Air conditioning of the Kiha 28 1500 series ====
The 4DQ generator set could supply only its own car, and on the two-engine Kiha 58 and Kiro 58 there was no room in the underfloor equipment to carry a 4DQ generator set. The simplified air-conditioning system did not reach practical use, and direct-drive air conditioning with a small bus engine was also examined, but the 4VK air-conditioning generator set — capable of supplying air-conditioning power for up to three cars including its own — was newly developed.

Engine — Daihatsu Diesel V-type 8-cylinder 4VK8.8 diesel engine (continuous rating 90 ps)
Generator — DM83 generator (two-pole)
Generating capacity — three-phase AC 400 V, 50 Hz, 70 kVA

4VK-based air conditioning began in 1969 (Showa 44). As it could not be fitted to the two-engine Kiha 58 and Kiro 58, the policy was adopted of fitting it to the single-engine Kiha 28 and Kiro 28. KE53 air-conditioning-control and KE8 power-supply jumper couplers were added to air-conditioned cars, including the Kiro 28 already air conditioned. Fitted cars were distinguished by adding 2000 to the original car numbers.

The 4VK engine was developed by doubling the cylinders in a V arrangement from a Daihatsu-manufactured truck in-line four-cylinder diesel engine, but its output and permissible rotational speed were somewhat insufficient to generate the 60 Hz power originally required for JNR's unit coolers, so it had to be operated with the somewhat inferior 50 Hz generator in effective generating capacity. Consequently, the effective air-conditioning performance of limited-express diesel railcars was somewhat lower than the catalog specification. It also had several drawbacks, such as emitting a constant shrill, piercing noise in operation, but in the end it became the standard air-conditioning engine for limited-express diesel railcars for many years afterward.

Kiha 28 1505–1510 were fitted with seven AU13 air-conditioning units and a 4VK generator set in fiscal 1968 (Showa 43), soon after being built, to supply power to the Kiro 58 on the Chuo Main Line, which as a two-engine car could not carry a 4DQ generator set. They also had an element of leading prototypes for 4VK-based air conditioning, and the underfloor 4VK generator set was arranged in the opposite direction to later converted cars. They were renumbered 2505–2510 in 1971 (Showa 46).
