==== Fitting 4VK sets to Kiha 28 air-conditioned cars without 4VK ====
In areas with few gradients such as the Boso district and on the Joban Line, there were also air-conditioned Kiha 28s without 4VK sets. As the Boso district's lines were electrified, except for the Kururi Line and Kihara Line, by 1975, cars transferred to other regions needing air-conditioning power were fitted with 4VK sets from fiscal 1975 as "Kiha car air-conditioning work F". The conversion did not extend to all cars; Kiha 28 24, 34, 38, 52, 54, 62, 71, 72, 75, 83 and 370 never had 4VK sets fitted until scrapping.

=== Distribution of air-conditioning power ===
The development of the 4VK power set brought the air conditioning of this series a certain degree of progress, but problems remained.

To air condition all cars, it is necessary to couple single-engine cars fitted with 4VK power sets at a ratio of one in three, but even where cars have air-conditioning units fitted, the units may not be operable depending on the formation.

In Formation A, three of the four cars are air-conditioned, so the air-conditioning power capacity can be secured, but the non-air-conditioned car sandwiched in the middle has no jumper couplers for air-conditioning control or power supply fitted, so the Kiha 58 air-conditioned car (B)'s air conditioning cannot be operated.

When the all-air-conditioned Formation B (five cars), incorporating two 4VK-generator-fitted cars, was coupled to the aforementioned Formation A, power supply and control for one car's air conditioning became possible from Formation B, enabling operation of the air conditioning of Formation A's Kiha 58 air-conditioned car (B). In other words, regardless of the orientation of the formation, up to three consecutive air-conditioned cars, including 4VK-generator-fitted cars, constitute one power unit.

However, Kiro 28 cars with self-supply 4DQ sets had control and air-conditioning power-supply jumper couplers added with the progress of ordinary-car air conditioning, so even if such a car was formed in the middle of a formation, as in Formation C, air-conditioning control and power supply could be relayed across it.

As securing generator sets and formation output was always a trade-off, after air conditioning the proportion of two-engine cars in this series' limited-express trains fell compared with the predecessor Kiha 55-series semi-express trains, and cases even arose where speed was forced to decline.

The DMH17H diesel engine fitted to this series had reached a certain standard in reliability, durability and quietness, but its basic design dated from the 1940s and was old-fashioned, with an output of 180 PS that was weak for the weight, and even with two fitted, performance did not reach that of electric cars. Moreover, after air conditioning, the combination of one Kiha 28 and one Kiha 58 (or Kiro 58) became mainstream, and the output per car was 275 PS, which was inadequate on gradient sections.

The Kiha 65, fitted with the newly developed DML30HS-series 500 PS-class engine and 4VK power set, was developed and built as a fundamental solution to the problem.

However, the Kiha 65 and the final-batch Kiro 28 cars fitted with 4VK generator sets were built in small numbers, and as they were prioritized for introduction on trunk and local lines west of the Chubu region, the air conditioning of diesel limited-express trains and the chronic output-shortage problem were not completely solved.

=== Cars not converted to air conditioning ===
Even in the 1990s and later, when many cars, including those for local trains, had been air conditioned, circumstances prevented air conditioning on routes with steep gradients for the following reasons.

As one example, Morioka Rolling Stock Center's Kiha 58s were allocated only as non-air-conditioned cars, except for Kiha 58 75, which formed a unit with the Joyful Train "Kenji" and training car Kiya 28 1. This was because the Hanawa Line, included in the operating section, is in a heavy-snow area and has a maximum gradient of 33.3 per mille between Matsuo-Hachimantai and Appi-Kogen stations; on a two-car formation under these conditions, even with one car single-engine, wheelspin when climbing could be caused by insufficient output and an insufficient number of driven axles, so the formation had to be all two-engine cars, making it impossible to secure air-conditioning power, and there was little point in operating with air-conditioning units that would only be dead weight. Also, the Yamada Line's climate is prone to the yamase winds, so non-air-conditioned cars survived for a long period.

== JNR-era conversions ==

=== JNR-era conversions involving renumbering ===

==== Kiroha 28 0 series ====
The Kiroha 28 was a type converted from the Kiro 28 into half-ordinary cars. There were the 0 series converted in the JNR era and the 100 series converted by JR West after privatization.

At the March 1975 timetable revision, a Green car was planned for the limited express "Awa" between Takamatsu and Tokushima on the Kotoku Main Line, but as a full-Green car was judged to be oversupply relative to demand, the Kiroha 28 0 series appeared in 1974 as a composite car converted to half ordinary seats. The conversion was carried out at Tadotsu Works.

A partition sliding door and wall were newly installed in the center of the saloon, and the rear side was converted to ordinary seats.

The ordinary-seat pitch was expanded from the 1,470 mm of other ordinary cars to 1,667 mm.

The window arrangement and seat spacing do not coincide.

Capacity was 24 Green seats and 40 ordinary seats.

The front-side conductor's room, Green saloon, rear-side toilet and washroom, air-conditioning units and 4DQ power equipment were left as on the donor car, without conversion.

Externally there was little change beyond the change of car number and the removal of the Green-car mark beside the ordinary-seat-side doorway.

Only one car of the type was allocated to Takamatsu Driving Office, transferring to Tokushima Diesel Car Depot (present-day Tokushima Driving Office) in 1977. It was demoted to Kiha 28 5301 in 1980, eliminating the type, and was scrapped in 1984.

==== Kini 28 and Kiyuni 28 ====
As replacements for the heavily aged Kiha 17 series (including the Kiha 44000 series) and the postal and baggage cars converted from the Kiha 55 series, conversion cars reusing the underframes and running gear of surplus Kiro 28s appeared from fiscal 1977. The all-compartment baggage car was the Kini 28 and the postal-baggage car the Kiyuni 28.

The bodies were newly built, of the same type as the Kiha 40 series built at the same period. As air-conditioning units were not fitted, the 4DQ power equipment and one each of the KE53 air-conditioning-control and KE8 high-voltage power-supply jumper couplers were removed. The conversions were carried out from 1978 at Nagoya, Tadotsu, Hata, Koriyama and Takasago Works, with Koriyama and Takasago handling the Kiyuni 28 only.

The Kini 28 had a baggage room of 12 t load behind the cab, with baggage shelves and a valuables box, and a baggage conductor's room, toilet and washroom at the rear car end.

The Kiyuni 28 had a 6 t postal room on the front side and a 6 t baggage room on the rear side, with toilet and washroom on the rear side face and the rear end face.

The livery of the first-delivered Kiyuni 28 1–6 was the general color of cream No. 4 and vermilion No. 4, but the other six cars were changed to the Tokyo metropolitan-area color of vermilion No. 5 following the October 1978 revision of the "Vehicle Livery and Marking Standards".

They were allocated throughout Japan except Hokkaido, but as railway postal and baggage transport was abolished at the November 1986 (Showa 61) timetable revision, less than ten years after conversion, all cars were scrapped by the following year, and not one car was inherited by the JR Group.

==== Kini 58 ====
To replace the two-engine Kini 55 and Kini 56 used on Joban Line freight trains, the Kini 58, based on the Kiro 58, appeared in 1978. As a two-engine car it had no space below the floor, so it differed from the Kini 28 in having the water tank installed inside the rear end face.

Nos. 1 and 2 were converted at Nagoya Works and No. 3 at Hata Works in 1978, and they were concentrated at Mito Engine Depot. On the Joban Line, an electrified route with dense train services, insufficient output and acceleration with a single DMH17-series engine was a problem, so two-engine cars were demanded. The Kini 55 was operated in common with the Kini 58 and was scrapped after the 1 February 1984 JNR timetable revision.

All cars were scrapped by February 1987 due to the abolition of freight transport.

==== Kiha 53 200 series ====
From the late JNR era in 1986 to after JR privatization in 1988, five Kiha 58s were converted to double-cab cars and incorporated into the Kiha 53 type. The conversion was carried out by cutting off the rear of the body and attaching a scrapped cab; the exterior resembles the Kiha 58003 transferred from Fuji Kyuko to the Arita Railway, but the window arrangement differs. The type was designated Kiha 53, which already existed on the Kiha 45 series, and a new sub-series was created to avoid duplication with existing cars. For a conversion of the same intent, there is the Kiha 53 500 series converted from the Kiha 56; see the Kiha 53 500 series (501–510).

To improve operational efficiency on the Rikuu East Line, which runs through snowy areas on gradients, the double-cab Kiha 53 200 series appeared in 1987. Two non-air-conditioned Kiha 58s were converted at Tsuchizaki Works (present-day Akita General Rolling Stock Center), with a toilet installed in the saloon. They were allocated to Kogota Transport District and operated on the Rikuu East Line and elsewhere, then transferred to Aizu-Wakamatsu Transport District. They were operated on the Tadami Line and scrapped in 2000.

=== JNR-era conversions not involving renumbering ===

==== Fitting of music sirens ====
As a level-crossing accident countermeasure, music sirens (special warning devices) were fitted as horns on twelve Kiha 58s in the Shikoku district between 1963 and 1965. The horn sound was an electronic tone of the scale "do-so-mi-do-do-so-mi-so-do", sounded at 7.5-second intervals, with speakers installed below the couplers. In fiscal 1964, two "whiskers", as on limited-express diesel railcars, were fitted to the front for identification purposes, making the cars easier to place at the head of formations.

The music sirens were later removed and the front end returned to the conventional specification. In 2008, just before JR Shikoku ended Kiha 58 series operation, "whiskers" were reproduced on Kiha 58 293.

==== Fitting of Joban radio antennas ====
Following the triple collision at Mikawashima Station on the Joban Line in May 1962 (the Mikawashima accident), train radio was to be installed on cars operated on the Joban Line from fiscal 1964 onward. This was carried out on the Kiha 58 series too, with two radio antennas fitted on the roof.

Cars air-conditioned after the fitting of the Joban radio antennas had unequally spaced air-conditioning units because of the equipment layout. Some air-conditioned cars transferred in from other lines did not have Joban radio antennas added, and as train radio spread nationwide in the late JNR era, the Joban radio antennas were progressively removed.

==== Bogie exchange with the Kiha 81 series ====
Of the Kiha 80 series, the Kiha 81 series built initially had a different brake system from the later Kiha 82 series, so work was carried out in fiscal 1969 to exchange the Kiha 81 series' bogies for the DT31B and TR68A, the same as the Kiha 82 series. The air-sprung DT27 and TR67 bogies released from the Kiha 81 series were transferred to the Kiha 58 series, being applied to 26 cars (some accounts say 24) of the Kiha 56 and 58 series. The DT22-series bogies released from the Kiha 58 series were transferred to exchange the Kiha 10 series' DT19-series bogies.

Conversions have been confirmed at least on Kiro 26 101; Kiro 28 81, 169, 503, 2112, 2125 and 2128; Kiha 28 2426; and Kiha 58 87, 100 and 269, but some cars, such as Kiro 26 101 and Kiro 28 2128, were later returned to the conventional DT22 series.

==== Front reinforcement work ====
To protect crew in the event of level-crossing accidents, conversions to reinforce the front of leading cars were carried out from fiscal 1975, and were started on the Kiha 58 series. On the Kiha 58 series, 4.5 mm steel plates were layered on the front waist panel; externally the thickness increased slightly, but there was no major change.

At JR East after privatization, front reinforcement work was actively promoted following the Narita Line Osuge level-crossing accident in 1991, and this series was also targeted. The work content differed by period and works, with examples where iron plates were used where stainless-steel reinforcement was applied elsewhere, and differences in whether anti-climbers were fitted.

==== Niigata Railway Administration air-horn conversions ====
A conversion applied to cars allocated within the jurisdiction of the Niigata Railway Administration, a heavy-snow area. A cylindrical cover was fitted to the air horn (typhon) to prevent snow from entering.

Fitted cars included Kiha 58 1022 + Kiha 28 2371, operated to the very last at Niitsu Transport District even after JR East inheritance, and, in cases where they were used as they were even after transfer to other districts, Kiha 58 75, allocated to Morioka Rolling Stock Center, and Kiha 28 2010, stored at Akita General Rolling Stock Center.

==== "Notoji" Romance Car conversion ====
To promote tourism and improve the image of the Noto region, work was carried out in 1980 on Kiha 28 2049 at Nanao Engine Depot (present-day Nanao Railway Department), used on the limited express "Notoji" on the Nanao Line: exchanging the seats and installing sightseeing-guide videos.

Carpet was laid on the floor and the seats exchanged for rotating cross seats like those of the 0-series Shinkansen, changing capacity to 44.

To show sightseeing-guide videos in the car while running, video playback equipment was fitted, with 50-inch video screens at the front and rear of the saloon and 24 side speakers on the side walls.

One window near the rear of the saloon was made smaller, and a symbol mark was placed beside the vestibule window.

One AU13 air-conditioning unit was removed, leaving six.

This was an experimental conversion to promote tourism in the corridor region, and from 12 July that year it was operated as ordinary reserved-seat cars, one round trip in busy seasons only, under the Romance Car name. However, the exterior remained in the JNR limited-express color, making visual distinction difficult, and passenger numbers did not increase, so operation ended in 1982. The video playback equipment was later removed, and the car was also used on local trains. The car was converted to Kiro 29 552, an intermediate insert car of the Golden Express Astor, in 1987.

==== Special preservation work ====
Entering the 1980s, limited-express diesel railcars, then 20 years from manufacture, began to show marked aging, but amid restraint on investment, special preservation work aimed at service improvement and safety was begun from fiscal 1981. The initial plan was for about 700 cars, with replacement of the lower body panels, rain gutters, toilets and washbasins.

==== Conversions for "Umineko" and "Murone" ====
On the Kita-Rias Line and Minami-Rias Line of the Sanriku Railway, which opened in 1984 as a third-sector railway, JNR cars were to make one round trip a day in the summer busy season, so accommodation conversions were carried out on the Kiha 58 series used on "Umineko" (Morioka–Miyako–Kuji) and "Murone" (Ichinoseki–Mori–Kamaishi).

Five cars were converted: Kiha 58 416, 486 and 1511, and Kiha 28 336 and 390. The livery was blue and ivory stripes representing the Sanriku sea and sky, and the seats were exchanged for rotating cross seats from scrapped 0-series Shinkansen cars.

Kiha 58 1511 and Kiha 28 390 were restored to conventional cross-seat ordinary cars, in line with engine replacement from fiscal 1989 after JR East inheritance, and the livery was changed to the Morioka color.

==== Tatami-room conversions for the Nagasaki area ====
In 1985, the following conversions were carried out on two cars, Kiha 28 2006 and 2114, then allocated to Nagasaki Engine Depot.

• Carpet was laid on the floor, and karaoke and mahjong tables installed.
• White shoji screens were fitted to the side windows.
• An original head mark, "Batten NAGASAKI", was fitted at the front.

Revenue operation began on 26 May 1985. In operation, a Kiha 58 was coupled in the middle, and they were used on small group trains; both cars were scrapped in December 1986.

==== Accommodation conversions for the Shikoku district ====
Accommodation-improvement conversions carried out at Tadotsu Works by the Shikoku District Bureau on surplus cars of this series generated by the reduction in limited-express operations in the late JNR era. Note that the conversions did not involve renumbering.

===== Group-exclusive cars =====
Between 1984 and 1985, conversions to the group-exclusive cars described below were carried out on three cars — Kiha 58 577 and 769, and Kiha 28 2475 — allocated to Takamatsu Driving Office.

• Seats and tables were exchanged for 0-series Shinkansen rotating cross seats, giving a capacity of 52.
• Karaoke equipment, speakers and a water dispenser were fitted.
• The exterior was changed to white with a blue wave pattern on one Kiha 58, and white with vermilion S-shaped lines on the other two cars.

They were used for group trains and as extra cars on limited expresses, but were demoted to ordinary cars in 1988 when "Tabidachi" and "Rainbow" appeared after JR privatization. On demotion, the exterior was changed to the JR Shikoku color, and the seats and tables were left unchanged, with only the karaoke equipment, speakers and water dispenser removed, and they were used on limited expresses like other ordinary cars.

===== Grade-up conversions =====
Conversions carried out between 1985 and 1986 on Kiha 58 1035 and Kiha 28 2476, allocated to Tokushima Diesel Car Depot (present-day Tokushima Driving Office).

• The livery was changed to white with vermilion S-shaped lines, as used for the group-exclusive cars described above.
• Kiha 58 1035's seats and tables were exchanged for 0-series Shinkansen rotating cross seats, and Kiha 28 2476's for Kiha 181-series rotating cross seats, giving a capacity of 60.

This conversion omitted the karaoke equipment and water dispenser of the group-exclusive cars and increased the seat capacity, premised on scheduled limited-express operation.

They were demoted to ordinary cars in 1988 when "Tabidachi" and "Rainbow" appeared after JR privatization. On demotion, the exterior was changed to the JR Shikoku color, and the seats and tables were left unchanged, and they were used like other ordinary cars. Kiha 28 2476 later had its toilet and washroom equipment removed and was semi-cross-seated in 1990.

==== Fitting of skirts to flat-window cars ====
Late-built panoramic-window cars had skirts from new, but some flat-window cars allocated in Shikoku and Kyushu were also given skirt-fitting conversions as a level-crossing accident countermeasure.

== Major conversions after JR privatization ==
After privatization, each company carried out conversions and refurbishments specialized to its operations and the lines on which cars were deployed.

=== JR East conversions ===
In addition to life extension through body refurbishment work and the special preservation work, many cars were semi-cross-seated to suit conditions on the lines where they were operated, but at JR East there were the following examples of major conversions without renumbering.

==== Engine replacement and fire prevention measures ====
At JR East, on-road testing of engines to replace the DMH17 series had been carried out from January 1988, but during this, in March of the same year, the Joyful Train "Salon Express Arcadia" suffered a fire accident. The cause was overheating of the exhaust pipe. Also, as countermeasures considering the aging of the DMH17H engines themselves and fuel-consumption problems, from September 1989 engines were replaced on Kiha 58-series cars and other DMH17-series-equipped cars such as the Kiha 52 and Kiha 35 series, with Niigata Engineering (DMF13HZ), Komatsu (DMF11HZ (SA6D125-H-1)) and Cummins (DMF14HZ (NTA855-R1)) engines.

These new engines were originally rated at 330 PS or 350 PS, but when replaced on DMH17-series cars the output was reduced to 250 PS to cope with the capacity limits of the reused conventional liquid transmissions.

==== Car refurbishment work ====
At JR East, car refurbishment work aimed at life extension began in 1990. The work included replacement of exterior panels, exchange of passenger doors and replacement of decorative panels, and seats were semi-cross-seated except in the Morioka area.

==== "Yoneshiro" and "Gassan" grade-up cars ====
To improve service on premium trains such as the limited expresses "Yoneshiro" and "Gassan", Kiha 58-series grade-up cars appeared in fiscal 1991. In addition to the usual refurbishment work, seats were exchanged for reclining seats, and electric direction blinds were fitted for the side destination indicators.

==== Conversion to training cars ====
At JR East, cars called "training cars" appeared for the periodic education and training of crew in handling abnormal situations and emergency measures. They were applied to surplus 103-, 113-, 115-, 455- and 485-series electric cars, but for diesel railcars, Morioka Rolling Stock Center cars of this series were converted at Tsuchizaki Works, mainly internally, with the removal of some seats, the installation of lockers and tables for storing supplies, and monitors and racks for carrying videos for audiovisual training. Externally, two white lines and "training car" markings were added to distinguish them from ordinary cars.

After conversion they remained allocated to Morioka Rolling Stock Center and were always operated forming a unit with Kiha 58 75, but were scrapped in November 2008, eliminating the type.

=== JR West conversions ===
Although engine replacement was not carried out, many cars received life-extension work. Cars used on limited-express services on local lines such as "Notoji" and "Miyoshi" had their seats changed and liveries altered. Cars for local lines often received one-man-operation conversion work and semi-cross-seating.

==== Life-extension N, NA and N40 work ====
The JNR-era special preservation work was continued at JR West as life-extension N work; from 1990, life-extension NA work was carried out on cars already given the special preservation work, aiming at further advanced life extension, and life-extension N40 work, anticipating 40 years of use after manufacture, was also carried out. These works included replacement of saloon decorative panels, renewal of toilets and washrooms, and renewal of wiring and piping.

==== Kiroha 28 100 series ====
The limited express "Sakyu" between Okayama and Tottori ran as a four-car formation including a Green car, but as the Green car's ridership was low, the Kiroha 28 100 series was converted at JR West's Tottori and Goto Works between 1987 and 1988, halving the Green car and making a three-car formation. The sub-series distinction of 100 was made to distinguish it from the Kiroha 28 0 series, which appeared in 1974 and was eliminated in 1980. The donor cars were all late-built model-change cars of the group with low gutter height.

A partition sliding door and wall were newly installed in the center of the saloon, and the rear side was changed to ordinary seats (box seats).

With the installation of the partition, the first window on the front side of the ordinary seats was made smaller and fixed. Thus, unlike the 0 series, the exterior also changed.

The ordinary-seat pitch was 1,605 mm.

The window arrangement and seat spacing do not coincide. Also, although scrapped parts were used for the seats, the Green seats were exchanged for an improved semi-bucket type.

Capacity was 28 Green seats and 40 ordinary seats.

Later, at the same time as the conversion of the Kiha 58 7200 series for "Sakyu" (see below), conversions were carried out, including exchanging the ordinary seats for Green-car rotating reclining seats and changing the livery, reducing the ordinary-seat capacity to 28.

Although not a 2000 series, as the donor cars were Kiro 28 2000 series, they continued to carry 4VK power equipment.

They were allocated to the Nishi-Tottori Rolling Stock Branch of Tottori Railway Department, but 101 and 102 were scrapped in 1998 following the abolition of "Sakyu" in November 1997. 103 and 104 transferred to Okayama Electric Car Depot Diesel Car Center (present-day Okayama Diesel Car District) and were used on the limited express "Tsuyama" between Okayama and Tsuyama, but were scrapped in 2004 due to aging.

== Conversions to Joyful Trains and sightseeing trains ==
This series had many crew and maintenance staff familiar with its handling, and by the 1980s many cars had air conditioning. Moreover, as diesel railcars, there were few constraints on operating sections and train length, making them suitable for conversions dedicated to group trains. Making use of these characteristics, group-exclusive cars converted from this series began to appear in various places from the late JNR era, and many Joyful Trains converted from this series, with salon-style interiors and tatami saloons, appeared at the JR companies after privatization, being operated in various forms as a revenue-increasing measure.

However, with changes in travel styles and economic downturns, and as even the last-built cars of this series were 18 years old at the time of JNR privatization in 1987, the overall age of the fleet became high, and conversion targets for Joyful Trains also shifted to the Kiha 40 series, which was newer than this series, so from the late 1990s many cars were scrapped due to aging. In this series, JR East Morioka Division's "Kenji" was scrapped in September 2018, and as of 2019 no cars remained in the JR Group as this series.

Some cars converted to Joyful Trains had their types changed from Kiha 56 and Kiha 58 to Kiro 59, Kiha 59, Kiha 27 and Kiha 28 to Kiro 29 and Kiha 29, and the Kisaro 59 — the only trailer car in the broad this series — was completed in this group. The Kisaro 59 was a car transferred from Type 12 passenger cars.

== Tests ==

=== Multiple-unit operation of electric and diesel railcars ===
In 1964 (Showa 39), a test of multiple-unit operation of electric and diesel railcars — a technical issue on the Joban Line — was carried out. The necessary main equipment was fitted, and couplers and gangway diaphragms for both electric cars and diesel railcars were modified (as in the original), and the test was conducted with a formation of eight 451-series cars and three Kiha 28 cars (plus two cars as dead weight). There were deemed to be no obstacles in practical terms, but as there were issues with crew operation and instructor training for electric and diesel railcars, and cars required conversion, the benefits of multiple-unit operation were deemed thin.

Next, in December 1966 (Showa 41), a multiple-unit test between the 165 series and the Kiha 58 was carried out between Tsuruta and Nikko on the Nikko Line. Coordinated-operation conversions were carried out on Kuha 165 and the Kiha 58, and the Kiha 58 was fitted with a brake changeover device. The test confirmed that coordinated operation of electric and diesel railcars was possible.

=== JR East's comparative test of refurbishment engines ===
At JR East, to select refurbishment engines to replace the DMH17 series, a long-term test was carried out between January and November 1988, with engines replaced on three Morioka Passenger Car Depot Kiha 58s. The targets were Kiha 58 614, 277 and 628, with two each of Cummins NTA855R1 on Kiha 58 614, Niigata Engineering DMF13HZ on Kiha 58 277, and Komatsu SA6D125H1 installed on each car. Engine output was set at 330 PS in all cases.

The test was carried out on the Kamaishi Line, Hanawa Line and elsewhere, and based on the results, full engine replacement was carried out on the Kiha 58 series, Kiha 52 and others. After the test, all three test cars were standardized on the DMF13HZ. During this test period, in March 1988, the Joyful Train "Salon Express Arcadia" fire accident occurred.

== History ==

=== Introduction to premium trains ===
In April 1961 the Kiha 56 series began revenue operation on the Nemuro Main Line's "Karigachi", in July the Kiha 57 series on the Shin'etsu Main Line's "Shiga", and in October the Kiha 58 series on the Chuo East Line and Oito Line's "Alps", in each case as limited-express trains.

Thereafter, the Kiha 56 and 58 series continued to be built in large quantities of 100–200 cars per year, and from their introduction until scrapping they were deployed in large numbers on trains in non-electrified sections throughout Japan, except Shizuoka Prefecture (although some cars were allocated to Numazu Engine Depot at delivery, they never actually entered service there and transferred after a very short period).

In the Boso area, where special timetables are arranged in summer for beachgoers, and in the Hokkaido area, busy in peak season, large numbers of extra and special trains are run, so this series was characterized by many formally allocated cars from new builds and transfers, in addition to cars borrowed from other regions. Many of these cars belonged to the relevant area's vehicle base for only the two to three summer months, transferring to other regions after the season ended.

New builds continued until fiscal 1969, in line with the JNR Modernization Five-Year Plan, and thereafter, for about 20 years from the 1970s, they were widely used on limited-express trains on trunk and sub-trunk lines, and on local trains at the ends of lines. However, with the advance of trunk-line electrification and the upgrading of limited-express trains to super expresses, diesel-railcar limited expresses gradually narrowed their sphere of operation. This series contributed greatly to the air conditioning of trains in regional districts in the 1970s, but entering the 1990s it became something of a presence left behind by the trends of the times in terms of in-car equipment. Its maximum speed was 95 km/h, which was sufficient for the many lines run by limited-express trains, including trunk lines.

Green cars began to become surplus in the mid-1970s, and the first scrapping occurred at the 10 March 1975 timetable revision. Some were converted to baggage cars and postal-baggage cars, and in the Shikoku district they were demoted to ordinary reserved cars at the 1 October 1980 timetable revision. At privatization, 21 Kiro 28s were inherited in total — seven by JR Central and 14 by JR West — of which 20 were final-batch cars of the 2300 and 2500 series with 4VK air-conditioning power equipment, and only 2162 from the long-formation 100 series. All 0-series cars were scrapped or converted to other types in the JNR era.

On the other hand, even into the 1980s there were still many multi-level trains performing complex divisions and couplings, and although reduced from their peak, limited-express trains with this series were still operated.

Limited expresses remained that ran entirely on electrified sections for reasons of vehicle supply and operations, such as "Shirayuki" between Kanazawa and Aomori, "Oga" between Ueno and Akita via the Ou Main Line, and "Akakura" between Nagoya and Niigata via the Chuo West Line, Shinonoi Line and Shin'etsu Main Line.

At the 15 November 1982 JNR timetable revision, accompanying the opening of the Tohoku and Joetsu Shinkansen, the many limited expresses in the Tohoku and Joetsu-Shin'etsu areas to which this series had been deployed became subject to rationalization: upgrades to super expresses, frequency reductions and abolition.

At the 14 March 1985 JNR timetable revision, Green cars were abolished in the Kyushu district, and many limited expresses were again upgraded to super expresses or downgraded to rapid trains, so a large number of surplus cars were generated compared with before, with the following tendencies.

• Transfer to local-train operation (see below).
• Use as donor cars for Joyful Train conversions.
• Cars continuing on limited-express and rapid service were given accommodation improvements, with seats exchanged for rotating cross seats or reclining seats.

Separately, to provide access to the site of the science exposition (Expo '85) held from 17 March to 16 September 1985, the temporary rapid "Expo Liner" was operated on the Joban Line, using surplus cars of this series from Mito Engine Depot that had been on the limited expresses "Tokiwa" and "Okukuji", abolished at the timetable revision three days before the opening.

Thereafter, from the 1990s to the early 2000s, nearly all diesel-railcar limited-express trains across the country disappeared, being abolished or upgraded to super expresses. The last scheduled limited express using this series was "Miyoshi" on the JR West Geibi Line, but it was abolished at the 1 July 2007 timetable revision.

=== Transfer to local and other trains ===
Although becoming surplus as a limited-express type, even in 1980 the earliest cars were less than 20 years old and had ample service life remaining. Some had already been used on local trains, mainly non-air-conditioned cars, but from the 1980s air-conditioned cars were also transferred in large numbers, being used to replace the aged, non-air-conditioned Kiha 20 and Kiha 55 series.

At the time, the Kiha 40 series, built to replace the aged Kiha 10 series, was unsuitable for gradient sections due to the compatibility of engine output and transmission settings and car-weight problems, whereas this series, being mainly two-engine cars, was easy to deploy on gradient sections, and, particularly west of the Chubu region, with many air-conditioned cars from limited-express use, maintained a reasonable standard of equipment, contributing greatly to the air conditioning of regional trains.

Cars also appeared with the following conversions specialized to the lines of operation, premised on local-train operation.

• Changing cross seats near the doors to longitudinal seats
• Further removal of the partitions between vestibule and saloon, and the toilet and washroom equipment
• One-man-operation-compatible cars after the privatization and breakup, etc.

== Operations ==
The Kiha 58 series began service on each line from 1961, and in the 1980s, with the contraction of limited-express trains, scrapping and transfer to local transport progressed. At the privatization and breakup of JNR in April 1987, this series (excluding the Kiha 56 and 57 series) was inherited by the five passenger JR companies, totaling 1,098 cars.

JR East: 323 cars
JR Central: 103 cars
JR West: 353 cars
JR Shikoku: 131 cars
JR Kyushu: 188 cars

After privatization they continued to be used on limited-express trains and local-line local trains as in the JNR era, and many conversions to Joyful Trains were also carried out. However, from the 1990s scrapping progressed due to replacement from aging, the abolition of limited-express trains, and the end of operations with the electrification of local lines.

One factor in this was the carcinogenicity problem of asbestos, which surfaced in 2005 and became an issue in many quarters. In Japan it had been used in many industrial products, and old railway vehicles also had many examples of its use in interiors and running equipment. Thus, adverse effects on maintenance staff were also discussed in the railway industry. This series was no exception, with asbestos used in car interiors and engine gaskets, and asbestos-scattering prevention work was barely carried out, also from the point of view of aging.

On 11 March 2011, the last scheduled operation of this series — between Toyama and Etchu-Yatsuo on the Takayama Main Line, by cars belonging to the JR West Toyama Regional Railway Department Toyama Driving Center — ended.

With the scrapping of the last stored JR East car on 30 November 2020, the type was eliminated from all JR companies.

=== East Japan area (JR East) ===
After privatization they were inherited by JR East, with dedicated liveries applied by allocated depot and line, and were operated mainly on local transport in the Tohoku and Shin'etsu regions. Scrapping progressed through replacement by the Kiha 100 and 110 series, Kiha E130 series and Kiha E120, or knock-on transfers from the introduction of new cars. The last scheduled operation, with three cars belonging to Niitsu Transport District, ended at the 14 March 2009 timetable revision.

From 2011, only the Joyful Train "Kenji" (Kiha 58 650 + Kiha 28 2010 + Kiha 58 1505), belonging to Morioka Rolling Stock Center, was operated on group trains, centered on the temporary rapid "Sanriku Train Miyako" between Morioka and Miyako (via the Yamada Line), mainly on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays outside winter, but it was scrapped in September 2018.

Thereafter, Kiha 58 75 — the last car with registered status across the whole of the JR companies, belonging to Morioka and stored as a reserve car at Akita General Rolling Stock Center — was also scrapped on 30 November 2020, eliminating the type.

==== Tohoku and the Ou Main Line ====
On the Tohoku Main Line, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Miyagi no" between Ueno and Sendai was renamed "Rikuchu" at the 1 October 1961 (Showa 36) San-Roku-To revision, with its extension to Morioka Station, and its cars were replaced with the Kiha 58 series. In December that year it became a three-level train, combined with the Kamaishi Line "Rikuchu" for Miyako and the semi-express "Dai-2 Hayachine" between Morioka and Kamaishi.

In May 1962 they were deployed on the temporary limited express "Dai-2 Bandai" between Ueno and Aizu-Wakamatsu on the Ban'etsu West Line, and the temporary semi-express "Iwashiro" between Koriyama and Aizu-Wakamatsu, which were made scheduled in June that year.

In July 1962 they were deployed on the limited express "Akebono" between Sendai and Aomori (via the Yokoguro Line and Ou Main Line), which became the first premium train on the Yokoguro Line (later the Kitakami Line). The "Akebono" Kiha 58 series was also operated in common with the Sendai–Akita semi-express "Tazawa". On the Uetsu Main Line, from April 1963 they were deployed on the limited express "Shirayuki" between Kanazawa and Aomori (via Niigata Station and the Hakushin Line), coupled with the limited express "Akebono" between Akita and Aomori.

At the October 1963 timetable revision, the limited expresses "Dai-1/Dai-2 Zaou" and "Iide" between Ueno and Yamagata/Niigata (via the Ban'etsu West Line) were newly established, and at the same time the passenger-car limited express "Dewa" between Ueno and Shinjo was diesel-carred and extended to Sakata via the Rikuu West Line. In March 1964 they were deployed on the limited expresses "Dai-2/Dai-1 Zaou/Bandai" between Ueno and Yamagata/Aizu-Wakamatsu, and "Mutsu" between Sendai and Aomori.

==== Morioka area ====
In the final years they belonged to Morioka Rolling Stock Center (Mori-Mori). Scheduled operation on the Yamada Line ended on 24 November 2007 with the introduction of the Kiha 110 series. Kiha 58 1504, 1514 and 1528 were transferred to Myanmar together with the district's Kiha 52. The remaining cars were stored within Morioka Station. All were transferred to and scrapped at Akita General Rolling Stock Center by March 2008.

Thereafter only the Joyful Train "Kenji" continued in operation, but it ended with a group train on 8 September 2018, ending all operation of the series held by JR companies, let alone the district.

The Joyful Train "Kogane" was allocated, but withdrew from service on 26 December 2010 due to aging and was exported overseas.

In the same month of June 1962, the temporary semi-express "Watarase" between Ueno and Takasaki (via Oyama Station and the Ryomo Line) began operation; "Watarase" was made scheduled at the October revision that year and became a three-level train, combined with the semi-express "Tsukubane" between Ueno and Mito/Moka. The division and coupling of "Watarase" and "Tsukubane" was carried out at Madara Station, and "Tsukubane" did not stop at Oyama Station, entering the Mito Line via the Oyama Shortcut Line.

==== Chuo East Line ====
On the Chuo East Line, at the San-Roku-To revision the semi-express "Alps" between Shinjuku and Matsumoto was upgraded to a limited express, and the Kiha 58 series was deployed on "Alps", "Kamikochi" and "Shirouma". In April 1962, through operation of the limited express "Kawaguchi" between Shinjuku and Kawaguchiko by Fuji Kyuko's Kiha 58001 and 002 began, coupled on the Shinjuku–Otsuki section with JNR cars: the limited express "Dai-1 Alps" on the down, and the semi-express "Kaiji" on the up. From June 1963, the Chuo East Line diesel limited-express Kiro 28s were replaced by two-engine Kiro 58s.

==== Niigata area ====
In the Niigata area, the Kiha 58 series was deployed on the limited express "Kitaguni" between Kanazawa and Niigata, which began operation at the 1961 San-Roku-To revision. In 1962 it was deployed on the limited express "Akakura" between Nagoya and Niigata. At the April 1963 revision, with the electrification of Kanazawa on the Hokuriku Main Line, the operating section of "Kitaguni" was extended to between Osaka and Niigata.

In the final years they were allocated to Niitsu Transport District (Ni-Nitsu) and operated on the Ban'etsu West Line, Yonesaka Line and elsewhere, ending scheduled operation at the 14 March 2009 timetable revision. Of these, Kiha 58 1022 + Kiha 28 2371, restored to the former JNR colors in 2003, continued to be used on event trains, and in autumn 2009, as part of a large tourist campaign in the Niigata area, they were also run on the Tadami Line, Iiyama Line and elsewhere, holding farewell operations with Kiha 52 on the Yonesaka Line on 12–13 December and on the Ban'etsu West Line on 26–27 December that year. On 12 January 2010 they were transferred under their own power to Koriyama General Rolling Stock Center and scrapped within that fiscal year.

=== Tokai area (JR Central) ===
JR Central's inherited cars were used on local transport on the Takayama Main Line, Kisei Main Line, Taketoyo Line and elsewhere, as well as on the limited expresses "Kasuga" and "Norikura" and the rapid "Mie". Until the December 1998 revision there were workings entering JR West territory with Mino-Ota Rolling Stock District cars. Operations ended in 2001, and from 2002 only Kiro 28 2303 remained registered, stored at Mino-Ota Rolling Stock District, but it was scrapped on 31 March 2008 and no cars remained. As a result the Kiro 28 type was eliminated. In February 2013 it was transported by road to Hamamatsu Transport District, and scrapped in October that year.

==== Chuo West Line ====
On the Chuo West Line, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Shinano" between Nagoya and Nagano was operated, but at the October 1961 San-Roku-To revision the Honshu Kiha 58 series was deployed for the limited expresses "Shinano", "Shinshu" and "Azumi". The Osaka–Nagano semi-express "Chikuma" was also diesel-carred, with the Shin'etsu Main Line Kiha 57 series deployed on it in common with Shin'etsu-system services.

==== Takayama Main Line ====
On the Takayama Main Line, in April 1963 the semi-express "Hida 2" between Nagoya and Kanazawa (via the Takayama Main Line) was upgraded to a limited express, and operated as "Kaetsu" on that section.

=== West Japan area (JR West) ===
In the West Japan area, even after the transfer to JR West, cars were deployed on limited-express operations, many of which ran for a while on lines such as the Sanin Main Line, but replacement and scrapping progressed due to the abolition of limited-express trains, the appearance of successor cars such as the Kiha 120 and Kiha 121/126 series, electrification on the Sanin Main Line between Kyoto and Kinosaki Onsen and on the Obama Line, and the aging of and falling demand for Joyful Trains.

The Tsuyama Line limited express "Tsuyama" was replaced from the Kiha 58 series to the Kiha 40 series at the 1 October 2003 revision. At the July 2007 revision, the Geibi Line limited express "Miyoshi" was abolished, and scheduled limited-express trains with the Kiha 58 series disappeared.

The Joyful Train "Honobono SUN-IN" ended operation in November 2009. Ordinary cars — Kiha 58 1114 + Kiha 28 2346 and Kiha 28 2360 + Kiha 58 477, belonging to the Toyama branch (Kin-Toya) of the Toyama Driving Center, Toyama Regional Railway Department — were used on the last scheduled operations of this series in Japan, between Toyama and Etchu-Yatsuo on the Takayama Main Line, from 14 March 2009, but operation ended on 11 March 2011. Thereafter only Kiha 28 2346 remained registered as a reserve car, and its transfer to the Isumi Railway was decided; it was scrapped on 24 July 2012, and on 9 October that year it was removed from Kanazawa General Rolling Stock Works toward Otaki Station (details below).

==== Hokuriku area ====
On the Hokuriku Main Line system, to coincide with the opening of the Hokuriku Tunnel in June 1962 and the electrification between Tsuruga and Fukui, the diesel limited express "Echizen" between Osaka and Kanazawa began operation.

With the 1963 electrification between Fukui and Kanazawa, "Echizen" was electric-carred, and the diesel limited express "Kitaguni" between Osaka and Niigata was established by integrating the passenger-car limited express "Tateyama" between Osaka and Toyama and the Niigata-area limited express "Kitaguni". The Osaka–Wakura/Noto semi-express/limited express "Okunoto", through to the Nanao Line, was also coupled to this train, and when coupled the formation had 12 cars including three Kiro 28s.

After the JR privatization they were also used on local trains on the Oito Line, Takayama Main Line (between Inotani and Toyama), Nanao Line and Obama Line, but scheduled operation ended with the Takayama Main Line in 2011.

==== Kansai area ====
On the Kisei Main Line system, the Kiha 55-series limited express "Kishu" between Nagoya and Tennoji was replaced with the Kiha 58 series from 1 March 1962. The Kiha 58 series was also deployed on the semi-express "Kinokuni" between Shirahama-guchi and Tennoji.

On local trains they were also used on the Katamachi Line and the Kansai Main Line.

==== Sanyo area ====
On the Sanyo Main Line system, at the October 1961 San-Roku-To revision the limited express "Miyajima" between Kyoto and Hiroshima was diesel-carred, and at the same time the limited express "Beppu" between Hiroshima and Beppu was newly established. The Kiha 58 series was also deployed on the Okayama–Hakata limited express "Sanyo", and on the Ogori–Hakata semi-express "Akiyoshi" it was used in a mix with the Kiha 55 series. In 1963, the Hiroshima–Nagasaki limited express "Debushima", coupled with the limited express "Beppu", also began operation.

They were also used on the Sanin–Sanyo connecting limited express "Chidori" and the Geibi Line limited expresses "Miyoshi" and "Taishaku", but with the abolition of "Miyoshi" in 2007, scheduled limited-express trains with the Kiha 58 series disappeared. Of the "Miyoshi" cars, Kiha 58 563 and Kiha 28 2329 were repainted to the former JNR colors at Shimonoseki Rolling Stock Center, Shimonoseki Regional Railway Department (present-day Shimonoseki General Rolling Stock Office), in October 2007, transferring from Hiroshima Driving Office to Okayama Diesel Car District; in November that year they were used on the "Mimasaka Slow Life Train" on the Imbi Line.

Kiha 58 563 and Kiha 28 2329 were also used on special trains in various places, including the Mine Line's "Oidemase Yamaguchi-gō", but withdrew from service after the "Arigatō Kiha 28/58" operated on the Tsuyama Line on 20–21 November 2010, and were later scrapped. Both cars are preserved at the Tsuyama Manabi no Tetsudokan in Tsuyama, Okayama Prefecture.

==== Sanin area ====
On the Sanin Main Line, at the San-Roku-To revision the semi-express "Hakuto" between Kyoto and Yonago was diesel-carred and upgraded to a limited express, with the Kiha 58 series deployed. From October 1962 the Kyoto–Taisha limited express "Daisen" (via the Hakubi Line) was diesel-carred, and from April 1963 this train had its Aioi–Okayama section changed to via the Ako Line, becoming the first premium train on the Ako Line.

In the Sanin area, almost all limited-express trains except those within the area used them: "Sanbe" ran as far as Kumamoto, "Taisha" as far as Nagoya, and there was the 14-car "Inaba", among others. Besides limited expresses, they were used on local trains on the end sections of "Chidori", "Sanbe" and "Misasa", and on the rapid "Tottori Liner", begun in time for the National Sports Festival, but scheduled operation ended at the 1 October 2003 revision with replacement by the Kiha 121/126 series under the Sanin Main Line speed-up project.

=== Shikoku area (JR Shikoku) ===
In the Shikoku area, the limited express "Shikoku" between Takamatsu and Uwajima, Shikoku's first limited express, began operation on 15 April 1961, initially with Kiro 28s incorporated into Kiha 55-series formations. At the 1 October 1961 San-Roku-To revision, the limited expresses "Dogo" (Takamatsu–Matsuyama), "Kuroshio" (Takamatsu–Suzaki) and "Urato" (Takamatsu–Kochi) were newly established, and the Kiha 55 series was progressively replaced with the Kiha 58 series.

The district's cars were inherited by JR Shikoku and operated mainly on local trains, but numbers were gradually reduced with the electrification of the Yosan Line between Takamatsu and Iyo-Shi, the introduction of successor 1000- and 1500-series cars, and the upgrading of limited expresses to super expresses with the introduction of the 2000 series and Kiha 185 series. Limited-express operation ended with "Yoshino-gawa", the last, when it was changed to the Kiha 185 series at the March 1998 revision (integrated into the super express "Tsurugisan" in 1999).

Operation on the Takamatsu branch of the Yosan Line ended at the 15 March 2008 timetable revision. The last remaining operation south of Matsuyama on the Yosan Line also ended on 15 October that year, ending all scheduled operation of this series and the Kiha 65. Thereafter, farewell operations were held as "Revival Trains" by Kiha 58 293 + Kiha 65 34 of Matsuyama Driving Office between 18 October and 2 November. At the same time, the "whisker livery" — identifying cars with electronic horns, adopted in the Shikoku district between about 1963 and 1969 — was restored.

On 12 December that year, two JR Shikoku-color cars were used in a comprehensive accident-response drill at Takamatsu Driving Office. All cars including these were scrapped on 31 March 2009.

=== Kyushu area (JR Kyushu) ===
In the Kyushu area, from July 1962 the Kagoshima Main Line limited express "Phoenix" between Hakata and Nishi-Kagoshima began operation with the Kiha 58 series. In October that year, the Nippo Main Line limited express "Aoshima" between Moji-ko and Miyazaki was diesel-carred, and "Phoenix" was also operated between Nishi-Kagoshima and Miyazaki. In the same October, the semi-express "Hikari" between Hakata/Moji-ko and Nishi-Kagoshima/Kumamoto was replaced from the Kiha 55 with the Kiha 58 series, and upgraded to a limited express for the first time in four years.

Throughout the JNR era and after the transfer to JR Kyushu, they were used on various lines in Kyushu, mainly non-electrified sections, but scheduled operation by Kagoshima General Rolling Stock Office (present-day Kagoshima Rolling Stock Center) cars ended at the 18 March 2007 timetable revision.

As of 1 April 2018, the following two cars remained registered.

Kiha 58 139 + Kiha 28 2401
Belonging to Kumamoto Rolling Stock Center, Kumamoto Railway Business Department. They were operated as "Aso 1962", the successor to "Aso BOY" — which ended operation with the laying up of the steam locomotive — from 22 July 2006 to 26 December 2010, but even after "Aso 1962" operation ended they were used on group and special trains. They were later preserved as reserve cars at Kumamoto Rolling Stock Center, but were transferred to Kokura General Rolling Stock Center in late March 2018. Kiha 28 2401 was scrapped on 16 January 2019, and Kiha 58 139 on 23 January that month.

Also, these two cars were the last registered cars of this series with original bodies and DMH17H engines across the entire JR Group.

== Sister cars ==
As examples of private railways ordering limited-express diesel railcars of the same type as JNR cars for the purpose of through operation into JNR lines, there is the case of Fuji Kyuko with the Kiha 58 series. Similar cases are seen with Nankai Electric Railway's Kiha 5501 and 5551, which ordered sister cars of the Kiha 55 series, and the Shimabara Railway's Kiha 55 and Kiha 26.

=== Fuji Kyuko Kiha 58 ===
From 1962 (Showa 37), the limited express "Kawaguchi", coupled with the Chuo Main Line limited express "Alps" from Otsuki Station on the Fuji Kyuko Line, ran through to Shinjuku Station. Although the Fuji Kyuko Line and the Chuo Main Line between Shinjuku and Otsuki were entirely DC-electrified sections, the coupled limited express "Alps" was necessarily a diesel train, as it ran through to non-electrified sections, so Fuji Kyuko needed its own dedicated cars for coupling, and Kiha 58001 and 58002 were built by Nippon Sharyo in December 1961 (Showa 36). In 1963 (Showa 38), Kiha 58003 was built as a spare car.

As the Chuo Main Line and Fuji Kyuko Line are steeply graded lines, with sections of 40 per mille, they were made Kiha 58 type with two engines, and although the exterior color and passenger accommodation were the same, they differed from JNR-specification cars in the following points.

• The car numbers were five digits, as on JNR former-type electric cars and former-type diesel railcars.
• As they normally formed two-car sets with Kiha 58001 and 58002, both cars were single-cab cars with toilet and washroom, the same as the JNR specification.
• Kiha 58003, from the viewpoint of a spare car, needed to be able to form on either side of a set, so it was built as the only double-cab car newly built in the Kiha 58 series. To match the capacity of single-cab cars while maintaining overall length and seat pitch, all passenger doors were narrowed in width and the vestibule shortened, and the space from abolishing the toilet and washroom was changed to four-person box seats, with the vestibule windows in that section made wide and large with fixed H rubber. Other external differences: there is no water tank on the roof; the front-side vestibule window is slightly narrower; and all passenger doors are compatible with the fitting of tablet protective frames.

From 1969 onward, JNR cars were progressively air conditioned, but Fuji Kyuko's cars were not air-conditioning converted, and with the electric-carring of all "Alps" trains in March 1975 they lost their purpose, and were scrapped on 24 April that year in exchange for the appearance of the Fuji Kyuko 5000 series. Thereafter, 58001 and 58002 had their toilets and washrooms removed, and all three cars were transferred in July that year to the Arita Railway, where through trains into JNR lines were also operated, beginning service in May 1976. They replaced that company's Kiha 07.

The Arita Railway Line is flat along its entire length, and from the viewpoint of reducing running costs, all cars were converted to single-engine at JNR Takasago Works in 1980. Also, as passenger numbers continued to decline, the double-cab 58003, capable of single-car operation, was often used, and with the start of operation of the air-conditioned Haimo 180-101 transferred from Tarumi Railway in June 1994, 58001 and 58002, whose utilization rate had long been falling, were scrapped in November that year. 58003 remained as a spare car until that railway's abolition in 2002.

== Transferred cars ==
As this series was used by JNR and then JR, the following seven cars in total were transferred to railway operators in Japan.

Kita-Kinki Tango Railway: 4 cars (see below)
Arita Railway: Kiha 58 136, Kiha 58 86
Isumi Railway: Kiha 28 2346 (see below)

There are also examples of transfer to the Sakhalin Railway of Russian Railways, the State Railway of Thailand and Myanmar Railways abroad.

=== Kita-Kinki Tango Railway KTR1000 and KTR2000 ===
In fiscal 1989, four cars of this series were transferred, for use on supplementary limited expresses to the KTR001 "Tango Explorer".

Types
KTR1000 (1001, 1002)
KTR2000 (2001, 2002)

KTR1000s were former Kiha 28s and KTR2000s former Kiha 58s; the type names derive from the number of engines carried.

Kiha 58 591 + Kiha 28 2198 → KTR2001 + KTR1001 (former owner: JNR Settlement Corporation)
Kiha 58 102 + Kiha 28 2314 → KTR2002 + KTR1002 (former owner: JR West)

Conversions carried out at the transfer: JR West Tottori Works carried out the work.

• The exterior livery was changed to silver metallic-based, with the corporate color Chitose-green plus Tobi-red lines below the windows.
• KTR1000s had their toilet and washroom removed and changed to a baggage space.
• Formation 2 (1002, 2002) had a front-end shape following JR West's Kiha 65 "Edel", and observation seats arranged stair-like.
• Formation 2's observation-room seats were exchanged for free-stop reclining seats with large back tables, with green seat moquette. The general-room seats of formations 1 and 2 were exchanged for rotating reclining seats modified from limited-express electric cars' simple reclining seats, with green moquette, as in the observation seats.

This type was named "Rainbow Resort", and also operated through into JR lines as three- or four-car formations, with formation 2 alone or formation 1 (1001, 2001) inserted in the middle, but KTR1002 and KTR2002 were scrapped and dismantled on 7 June 1995, and KTR1001 and KTR2001 on 24 January 1996, replaced by the new KTR8000 "Tango Discovery".

=== Isumi Railway Kiha 28 2346 ===
On 27 August 2012, the company's then-president Ryo Torizuka announced the transfer from JR West on his blog, and the car was delivered on 11 October that year.

Unlike Kiha 52 125, it was maintained at Kanazawa General Rolling Stock Works and repainted from the Takaoka color to the JNR limited-express color before transfer, then maintained again on the Isumi Railway. Revenue operation began on 9 March 2013. In revenue operation it forms a train with Kiha 52 125 and is coupled on the Ohara Station side.

The car was built as Kiha 28 346 by Teikoku Sharyo in 1964 and newly allocated to Yonago Engine Depot (present-day Goto General Rolling Stock Office) on 15 April that year. On 24 May that year it transferred to Niigata Engine Depot (present-day Niigata Rolling Stock Center), on 14 July to Chiba Diesel Car Depot, where it was used for beachgoer transport in the Boso area, and on 17 September back to Yonago Engine Depot — in effect loan-like transfers. In 1972 it was air-conditioned and fitted with a 4VK generator set, and renumbered 2346. It continued to be used in the Sanin area. In 1985 it transferred to Nanao Engine Depot (present-day Nanao Railway Department), and was inherited by JR West at privatization. In 1991 it transferred to Toyama Driving Office, and in 1996 to Takaoka Railway Department. In 2000 it transferred once to Obama, but with the electrification of the Obama Line in 2003 it transferred to Takaoka again. It later became a reserve car, but in 2004 it was loaned to Echizen-Ono Railway Department and used for disaster restoration on the Etsumi-Hoku Line. After this it always formed trains with Kiha 58 1114, and in 2007 transferred to Toyama with a trial increase in trains on the Takayama Main Line. It was operated on the Takayama Main Line in the Takaoka color.

As of 2022, it was the only operating car of this series in revenue service in Japan, but scheduled operation ended on 27 November 2022; the full inspection — costing about 100 million yen for parts re-manufacture and other work — was abandoned, support was sought by crowdfunding, and as of February 2024 it is statically preserved at Kuniyoshi Station, but from February 2024 crowdfunding was again carried out for panel beating and repainting, as rust from body corrosion and paint deterioration had become severe. Furthermore, in future the Isumi Railway plans experiential riding and driving experiences using these two cars and the Kiha 58, JNR-type diesel railcars, and has announced that, while aiming at the "Rail Park" concept — the development of a tourist facility where people can enjoy railway vehicles — it will target new promotion of railway use and the development of tourist demand using these vehicles, which are also Showa-era industrial heritage.

=== Exports abroad ===
Given this series' versatility and large numbers, there were cars donated free of charge abroad after scrapping. From JR East they were donated to Russia's Sakhalin Oblast, and from JR West to Thailand and Myanmar. There are also cars exported from JR West to the People's Republic of China, but they have been left abandoned at their destination.

==== Russian Federation Ministry of Transport (Sakhalin Railway) ====
At the Far Eastern Railway Sakhalin Branch of the Soviet Ministry of Transport, ten D2-series trains (40 cars) built by Fuji Heavy Industries were introduced in 1985 via Nissho Iwai to replace Japanese-made A1-series diesel railcars (introduced 1963), and used for commuter passenger transport; after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the Sakhalin Railway of the Russian Federation Ministry of Transport inherited them, but with high inflation and budget shortages from the economic chaos after democratization, parts could not be procured, and maintenance of the D2 series became difficult.

In August 1992, a delegation of railway engineers from JR East and others visited the Sakhalin Railway, and in January 1993 a Sakhalin Railway delegation visited Japan and toured JR East and JR West stations, travel centers and works; this was the impetus for the signing of a free vehicle-transfer contract between the Sakhalin Railway and JR East in October that year, and 29 Kiha 58s were exported from Ichihara Port, Chiba Prefecture, to Kholmsk Port.

After arrival locally, they were transferred under their own power from Kholmsk–Sol'tsilovochny Station to the Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk Engine Depot, and 17 cars, excluding parts-donor cars, were maintained. As the K-1 type (K-01 onward), they began operation on commuter passenger trains from April 1994. With the recovery of the Russian economy, the budget shortage was resolved, and all cars ended operation in 2000 when the D2 series returned to service. One car is statically preserved.

==== Thailand ====
In 1997, a total of 26 cars — 14 Kiha 58, 9 Kiha 28 and 3 Kiro 28 — and in 1999 a total of 20 cars — 11 Kiha 58 and 9 Kiha 28 — 46 cars in all, were donated free of charge.

The State Railway of Thailand carried out modifications including re-gauging to 1 m, changes to the brake system, and the fitting of steps at the doors. Local type names: former Kiha 58s became the 100 series, former Kiha 28s the 200 series, and former Kiro 28s the 300 series.

Initially they were used on premium trains, but around 2000 the engines were removed and the air conditioning stopped being used, and they came to be used on local trains as substitutes for third-class passenger cars. Today the cabs and engines have been completely removed and the air conditioning is unused. The following causes are estimated.

• The cabs are on the opposite side from the local standard, making them awkward for recognizing signals and handing over staff and tokens.
• They were already aged and heavily deteriorated.
• The formations were haphazard, preventing appropriate operation; the discontinuation of air conditioning also stemmed from this.
• The bodies were large, exceeding the State Railway of Thailand's loading gauge, causing problems in tunnels and on sharp curves.

Later, large-scale refreshment work — cab removal and door relocation — was carried out on some cars. Until around 2005 they were repainted to gray with blue and white gradients (end faces plain yellow) and used on passenger trains in the Bangkok metropolitan area, but today most cars are laid up or scrapped. However, some cars are used as service vehicles, and with the aim of replacing aging old passenger cars, improvement work shortening the car bodies to cope with sharp curves has been carried out on some cars, though it has not led to service.

Separately from the above cars, the transfer of the "Resort Saloon Festa" was also planned, but was canceled for reasons on the Thai side. The severe aging of the donor cars was also a factor.

Reference site: State Railway of Thailand Friends Association — Wayback Machine (5 April 2003 archive)

==== Myanmar ====
In 2008, three Kiha 58s were donated free of charge by JR East. After transfer, large-scale conversion work was carried out, including re-gauging to 1 m gauge, lowering the roof height in view of Myanmar Railways' loading gauge, and removal of the air-conditioning units. Initially they were used on limited-express trains, and today they are used on Yangon suburban trains. Even before this, cars had been donated by JR West.

==== China ====
Kiha 28 2306 and Kiha 28 2486, exported after scrapping in 2004, have been confirmed to have been left abandoned for a long time in the bonded zone of Tianjin Port at two points in 2013 and 2018.

== Accident write-offs ==
Nine cars were written off in accidents, including during the JNR era and after JR privatization. For details of the accidents, see the linked pages.

Kiha 58 666
The car involved in the limited express "Yoshino-gawa" derailment accident that occurred on 14 October 1969. Formed at the head, the car collided with a dump truck and derailed heavily. Scrapped on 12 March 1970.

Kiha 58 1034
On 15 May 1973, while operating on the Nagoya–Tennoji limited express "Kishu 1", it collided with a dump truck at a level crossing between Sana and Tochihara on the Kisei Main Line. The car, formed at the head, suffered major front damage. Scrapped on 8 March 1974.

Kiha 58 409, 1015; Kiha 28 2005, 2352
The train involved in the Noto Line train derailment accident that occurred on 11 July 1985; the four-car limited express "Notoji 5". All cars were scrapped on 1 October that year.

Kiro 59 508
The car involved in the Salon Express Arcadia fire accident that occurred on 30 March 1988; it was completely burned out from a fire caused by exhaust-pipe overheating and scrapped.

Kiha 58 1023
The car involved in the Shigaraki Kogen Railway train collision accident that occurred on 14 May 1991. The car was formed at the head of the special train "Sekai Tōgeishi Shigarakigō", a three-car train of this series through-operated from JR West to the Shigaraki Kogen Railway. Between Onoya Signal Field and Shigarakigūshi-ato Station on the Shigaraki Line, it collided head-on with a four-car Shigaraki Kogen Railway SKR200-series diesel railcar formation and derailed heavily. As the body was bent, restoration was difficult, and it was scrapped on 31 March 1994.

Kiha 28 3013
On 26 August 2003, while operating on Dosan Line local train 226D from Kochi Station to Awa-Ikeda Station, the driver noticed that the 4VK engine for air-conditioning power was rotating faster than usual; near Gomen the driver tried to stop the 4VK engine but could not, and it was stopped by a maintenanceman waiting at Tosa-Yamada Station, but white smoke flowed into the car. A fire broke out from the floor at Awa-Kawaguchi Station, and passengers were evacuated and firefighting carried out.

The cause was that a part of the 4VK engine came off, causing over-supply of fuel and abnormal combustion, which abnormally overheated the muffler; however, as replacement of this type was progressing, repairs were not carried out, and after being laid up it was scrapped on 31 March 2004.
